data.title: I got fooled by AI-for-science hype–here's what it taught me
data.author: qianli_cs
data.article_summary: 文章由物理学家Nick McGreivy撰写，讲述了他对AI加速科学研究的期望如何落空。McGreivy曾希望利用AI解决等离子物理中的偏微分方程（PDEs），但发现AI方法的效果远不如宣传的那样好，许多声称AI优于传统数值方法的研究存在不公平比较和数据泄露问题。尽管AI在科学领域的应用迅速增加，但他认为AI对科学的实际影响可能被夸大，科学界正面临可重复性危机。他警告说，AI在科学中的成功可能不如表面看起来那样显著，科学家们倾向于采用AI更多是为了自身利益，而非科学进步。最终，他对AI是否能逆转科学生产力下降的趋势持怀疑态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI在科研和实际应用中的效果及其局限性的不同看法，以及对AI研究领域现存问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **AI是否带来实质性进展**：
  - **plasticeagle**认为，尽管很多人宣称AI将带来重大发现，但实际并未看到AI在任何领域带来显著的突破或渐进式改进，质疑AI是否仅是重新包装现有知识。
  - **Flamentono2**则持相反观点，认为AI已经在多个方面带来了突破性进展，例如图像生成和代码自动生成，并强调AI在提高科研效率方面的潜力。

• **AI研究中的问题**：
  - **nicoco**指出，AI领域并非唯一存在夸大宣传的领域，整个科研出版体系都存在类似问题，负面的结果往往不被发表。
  - **sublimefire**提到，AI相关研究的论文质量参差不齐，许多结果难以复现，模型更新换代快，导致难以验证研究结论的普适性。

• **AI对社会和工程技术的影响**：
  - **therebase**认为，讨论不应仅限于AI带来的技术成果，还应关注其对人类社会的影响，引用了关于AI侵蚀工程技术的文章。

• **科研激励机制和职业化问题**：
  - **rhubarbtree**认为，学术界的问题如追求引用和职业主义，同样体现在AI研究中，这些问题导致科研不再以追求真理为核心。

• **对AI工具的合理期望和使用**：
  - **omneity**指出，原文对AI的批评主要集中在特定架构（如PINN）的过度宣传上，而非全盘否定AI在科学计算中的作用。
  - **tonii141**和**pawanjswal**强调，AI并非万能，正确理解神经网络的数学基础和适用场景是有效使用这些工具的关键。

补充讨论：
• **科研激励和误导问题**：
  - **raesene9**和**KurSix**提到，理解科研人员的激励机制有助于识别潜在的误导性言论，并将AI研究中的问题与可重复性危机相比较。

• **AI在科研中的实际应用**：
  - **shalmanese**认为，文章实际上反映了学术界对如何正确解读学术声明的素养问题，强调科学输出是复杂社会技术系统的产物，需要经验积累来正确评估。

争议焦点：
• AI是否在实际科研和应用中带来了与其宣传相符的实质性进展，以及AI研究中夸大宣传和难以复现结果的问题是否比其他科研领域更为严重。

I’m excited to publish this guest post by
Nick McGreivy
, a physicist who last year earned a PhD from Princeton. Nick used to be optimistic that AI could accelerate physics research. But when he tried to apply AI techniques to real physics problems the results were disappointing.
I’ve
written before
about the Princeton School of AI Safety, which holds that the impact of AI is likely to be similar to that of past general-purpose technologies such as electricity, integrated circuits, and the Internet. I think of this piece from Nick as being in that same intellectual tradition.
—Timothy B. Lee
In 2018, as a second-year PhD student at Princeton studying
plasma physics
, I decided to switch my research focus to machine learning. I didn’t yet have a specific research project in mind, but I thought I could make a bigger impact by using AI to accelerate physics research. (I was also, quite frankly, motivated by the
high
salaries
in AI.)
I eventually chose to study what AI pioneer Yann LeCun later
described
as a “pretty hot topic, indeed”: using AI to solve partial differential equations (PDEs). But as I tried to build on what I thought were impressive results, I found that AI methods performed much worse than advertised.
The author, Nick McGreivy.
At first, I tried applying a widely-cited AI method called PINN to some fairly simple PDEs, but found it to be unexpectedly brittle. Later, though dozens of papers had claimed that AI methods could solve PDEs faster than standard numerical methods—in some cases as much as a
million times faster
—I discovered that a large majority of these comparisons were unfair. When
I compared
these AI methods on equal footing to state-of-the-art numerical methods, whatever narrowly defined advantage AI had usually disappeared.
This experience has led me to question the idea that AI is poised to “
accelerate
” or even “
revolutionize
” science. Are we really about to enter what DeepMind
calls
“a new golden age of AI-enabled scientific discovery,” or has the overall potential of AI in science been exaggerated—much like it was in my subfield?
Many others have identified similar issues. For example, in 2023 DeepMind
claimed
to have discovered 2.2 million crystal structures,
representing
“an order-of-magnitude expansion in stable materials known to humanity.” But when
materials
scientists
analyzed these compounds
, they found it was “
mostly junk
” and “respectfully” suggested that the paper “does not report any new materials.”
Separately, Princeton computer scientists
Arvind Narayanan
and
Sayash Kapoor
have
compiled a list
of 648 papers across 30 fields that all make a methodological error called
data leakage
. In each case data leakage leads to overoptimistic results. They argue that AI-based science is facing a “reproducibility crisis.”
Yet AI adoption in scientific research has been
rising sharply
over the last decade
. Computer science has seen the biggest impacts, of course, but other disciplines—physics, chemistry, biology, medicine, and the social sciences—have also seen rapidly increasing AI adoption. Across all scientific publications,
rates of AI usage grew
from 2 percent in 2015 to
almost 8 percent in 2022
. It’s harder to find data about the last few years, but there’s every reason to think that
hockey stick growth has continued
.
To be clear, AI
can
drive scientific breakthroughs. My concern is about their magnitude and frequency. Has AI really shown enough potential to justify such a massive shift in talent, training, time, and money away from existing research directions and towards a single paradigm?
Every field of science is experiencing AI differently, so we should be cautious about making generalizations. I’m convinced, however, that
some
of the lessons from my experience are broadly applicable across science:
AI adoption is exploding among scientists less because it benefits science and more
because it benefits the scientists themselves
.
Because AI researchers almost never publish negative results, AI-for-science is experiencing
survivorship bias
.
The positive results that get published tend to be overly optimistic about AI’s potential.
As a result, I’ve come to believe that AI has generally been less successful and revolutionary in science than it appears to be.
Ultimately, I don’t know whether AI will reverse the decades-long trend of
declining scientific productivity
and stagnating (or even decelerating) rates of
scientific progress
. I don’t think anyone does. But barring major (and in my opinion unlikely) breakthroughs in advance

data.title: Ann, the Small Annotation Server
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了名为Ann的社交注释工具，它基于ActivityPub协议，支持去中心化的网页注释功能。用户可以通过Ann存储、发送和接收注释，类似于评论、推荐或点赞。与传统社交媒体不同，Ann本身只是一个服务器，需结合前端应用使用。应用场景包括：在Gemini浏览器或博客中添加评论区、科研部门内部共享论文、获取关注者的文章推荐、通过浏览器插件查看和添加注释、用于AI训练的注释网络、以及作为插件集成到LibreOffice、Logseq等工具中。Ann的目标是让各种应用轻松集成社交功能，避免对中心化服务和JavaScript、追踪器的依赖，同时尊重用户隐私和选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个名为"Ann"的工具（可能与网络注释和社交注释相关）的可行性、创新性及其实际应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• **okonomiyaki3000**认为，类似工具自1997年以来每隔5年就有人提出，暗示这种概念并不新颖，可能缺乏独特性或实际突破。
• **MortyWaves**指出，"Ann"的功能与WebMentions非常相似，暗示其可能并无创新，只是已有技术的另一种实现。
• **staz**对工具的具体实现表示困惑，指出缺乏源代码或下载链接，并质疑该项目是否仅停留在概念阶段。
• **nashashmi**提到谷歌曾有过类似的实现（Sidekick），进一步支持了这种工具并非新概念的观点。
• **JellyBeanThief**热情支持网络注释的广泛应用，认为应允许用户在任何网页上自由注释并分享，强调这种工具应脱离内容托管方控制，具有开放性和中立性。
• **robertlagrant**简单表达了对该想法的赞赏，认为其有潜力。
• **wdbm**提出了与现有工具hypothes.is的比较，质疑"Ann"的独特优势。
• **sneak**支持社交注释功能，但担心如果该工具变得流行，浏览器可能会采取措施限制其使用，暗示技术实现和推广可能面临阻力。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：该工具的创新性和实际应用价值受到质疑，许多人指出类似工具和概念早已存在，且其实际应用和可持续性有待观察。
• **技术实现**：staz对工具的实际可用性表示怀疑，因为缺乏源代码或实际服务器。
• **应用场景**：JellyBeanThief描绘了广泛的应用场景，强调注释工具应具有开放性和中立性，但这一愿景可能面临技术和政策上的挑战。
• **市场竞争**：wdbm提到hypothes.is作为一个现有竞争者，引发对"Ann"竞争力和差异性的思考。
• **推广阻力**：sneak担心浏览器可能会对流行注释工具进行限制，暗示技术推广中的潜在障碍。

Ann, the Small Annotation Server
Ann is a minimal ActivityPub-based decentralised alternative social media built around
Web Annotations
. An annotation can be thought of as a comment, recommendation or a like on any piece of content. Ann allows you to store your annotations, send annotations to your followers and receive annotations from people that you follow.
Ann is different from other social medias and federated social medias. It is not really meant to have a single webpage you go to where you see all your "Ann related content" (though you could build that). Instead, it is just a server, so on it's own it's not very usable. What does get cool is when you connect it to front-end applications, so for example some applications could be:
A comment section in a
Gemini
browser or for your blog.
A research department could have a private setup where they comment and share papers.
Get article recommendations from people you follow.
A web browser plugin that allows you to view other people's comments on content all around the web and add your own comments.
A network of annotated content that can be used for AI training.
A org mode/obsidian/logseq plugin to enable commenting and sharing files.
A hashtag or a reposting user to follow that enables people to share/like/comment recommendations, essentially recreating Reddit and Hackernews.
Many applications, from LibreOffice, Logseq to video players could all benefit from having social functions to compete with centralised solutions like Notion, YouTube etc. Expecting each of these to implement servers for comments and annotations is not realistic. However with a self-hosted annotation server, these apps would only need to implement one integration and users would only need to be connected to a single server. My vision with Ann is a web that is not dependant on having "web apps" with Javascript and trackers, but instead enable embedding annotation capabilities to our favourite applications in a way that gives us choice of how we want to consume content, respects our privacy and keeps us in control.

data.title: Experimentation Matters: Why Nuenki isn't using pairwise evaluations
data.author: Alex-Programs
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种新的语言翻译质量基准测试方法的实验过程。作者最初使用简单的评分系统，让语言模型（LLM）为其他模型的输出打分（1-10分），并考虑了连贯性指标。随后，作者尝试使用成对评估和Bradley-Terry模型进行新基准测试，但遇到了成本高昂且效果不佳的问题，无法从噪声中提取出有效信号。经过多次尝试和调整，作者设计了一种折中方案，结合了成对评估和传统评分方法，通过循环处理句子、多模型翻译、多评估系统打分并进行统计分析，最终实现了一种更便宜且能获得较好p值的系统。该系统在一次德语测试中仅花费了6美元。

44007373.article_content:
Experiments with pairwise evaluations
Nuenki's old language translation quality benchmark used a simple system where a suite of LLMs would score the outputs of other LLMs between 1 and 10. There was a little additional complexity - namely, the coherence metric - but that was the gist of it. If you're interested in more details, take a look at the
previous blog posts
.
I've spent the last
week or so
working on a new benchmark using pairwise evaluations and a Bradley-Terry model. I documented some of the issues I was having with cost, and implemented the fixes.
I then spent 100 USD attempting to run enough comparisons to get the P-values to reduce and the model to find some actual signal from the noise. It didn't work, and it's not even close. Further improvement follows diminishing returns. The changes I discussed in the last blog post helped, but are nowhere near enough. It would take many hundreds to thousands of dollars to do a single experiment on a single language.
This leaves me with a dilemma: Yes, I narrowly prefer pairwise comparisons from a scientific perspective, but I can't get any useful data if I can't afford to run any experiments.
A compromise system
I built a new system that combines the two. It works, roughly (you can look in
the repo
if you're curious) by:
Iterating over the ~160 sentences
Translating the sentence with all of the tested models
Iterating over the 6 translation evaluation systems
Telling them to judge each separate translation by various factors, rank them, and score them from 0-100
Combining those scores and doing statistics on them
There are of course various controls (e.g. consolidating multiple translations into one when there are duplicates, randomising the order, and making the test blinded).
This system is a lot cheaper while also getting results with fairly good p-values! It differs from the old system in that it relies on only a single metric, rather than three, and isn't completely blinded - the comparison models see all the different translations when scoring. Here are the results of an early test run on German that cost ~6 USD. You can click on a row to view p-values!
P.S. If you'd like to learn a language while you browse the web, give
Nuenki
a try!

44007373.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种新的语言翻译质量基准测试方法的实验过程。作者最初使用简单的评分系统，让语言模型（LLM）为其他模型的输出打分（1-10分），并考虑了连贯性指标。随后，作者尝试使用成对评估和Bradley-Terry模型进行新基准测试，但遇到了成本高昂且效果不佳的问题，无法从噪声中提取出有效信号。经过多次尝试和调整，作者设计了一种折中方案，结合了成对评估和传统评分方法，通过循环处理句子、多模型翻译、多评估系统打分并进行统计分析，最终实现了一种更便宜且能获得较好p值的系统。该系统在一次德语测试中仅花费了6美元。

data.title: A man who visited every country in the world without boarding a plane (2023)
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: Torbjørn Pedersen, a Danish adventurer, achieved a unique world record by visiting every country without flying, a journey that took 10 years. Inspired by childhood dreams of adventure and motivated by the desire to accomplish a significant feat, Pedersen meticulously planned his trip, funded by savings and donations, while promoting the Danish Red Cross. Despite facing challenges like cerebral malaria and being held at gunpoint, he adhered to strict rules: spending at least 24 hours in each country, not returning home, and avoiding air travel. Pedersen's extensive international experience, from working in logistics across various countries to serving as a UN peacekeeper, equipped him with the resilience and adaptability needed for this monumental task. His journey, filled with highs and lows, also included personal milestones like getting married during the trip. Pedersen's story is one of determination and a passion for showcasing the positive aspects of every nation he visited.

‘Never, ever give up’… Torbjørn Pedersen in Sri Lanka in 2023.
Photograph: Mike Douglas
View image in fullscreen
‘Never, ever give up’… Torbjørn Pedersen in Sri Lanka in 2023.
Photograph: Mike Douglas
Travel
This article is more than
1 year old
Interview
Take the high road: the man who visited every country in the world – without boarding a plane
This article is more than 1 year old
Rachel Dixon
At 34, Torbjørn Pedersen embarked on a seemingly impossible journey that would take 10 years – and involve cerebral malaria and being held up at gunpoint. He reflects on the highs, the lows and the joy of getting married en route
Wed 16 Aug 2023 00.00 EDT
Last modified on Wed 16 Aug 2023 05.41 EDT
Share
T
orbjørn Pedersen has always dreamed of being a famous adventurer. He spent his childhood building dens in the woods, pretending to be his hero, Indiana Jones. Even as an adult, he couldn’t shake the sense that he was destined for greatness.
There was just one problem. “I was born at least 100 years too late,” he tells me over video call from his home in Copenhagen. “I had a profound feeling that everything had been done. The great adventures took place in the past. It was all over.”
Things reached a tipping point in 2013. He was 34 and had a successful career in shipping and logistics. He had just bought a flat and started a serious relationship. It was time to give up his childish dreams. Then his dad sent him an article about people who had travelled to every country in the world. “I didn’t know you could do that,” he says. “Certainly you would have to be a millionaire.”
But here were ordinary people walking, cycling and hitchhiking around the globe on shoestring budgets. Then came his eureka moment: “I discovered that no one had ever gone to every country in the world completely without flying [in one unbroken trip].” (A British man,
Graham Hughes
, has set foot in every country without flying, but took two breaks from the journey for personal reasons.)
View image in fullscreen
‘The high from entering a new country was the best feeling in the world’ … Pedersen in Ethiopia in 2017.
Photograph: Supplied image
Pedersen was already obsessed with world firsts: “The first to go to the north pole, the south pole, the deepest sea, the highest mountain, the longest river.” Now he had a chance to set a world record himself. “It was right in front of me,” he says, eyes gleaming. “It could be Ibn Battuta, Marco Polo … Thor Pedersen! I could do something of significance with my life, something worth putting in a book, something worth remembering. And it would be a great adventure!”
Pedersen spent the next 10 months planning the journey – the route, budget, what to pack – without ever making a conscious decision to go. It was only when he turned down an opportunity to work in South America that he realised he was fully invested in the project, as he had started to call it. He set himself three rules: at least 24 hours in each country; no visits home; and absolutely no flying. His list of countries included the 195 states recognised by the UN, plus extras such as Kosovo and Taiwan – 203 in total. He figured the journey would take him about four years. His budget was $20 a day, funded by savings, supporter donations and sponsorship. He would be acting as a goodwill ambassador for the Danish Red Cross, raising awareness of its work in 199 countries and encouraging people to give blood. He also aimed to
share something positive about every single country
– “even the ones we hear horrible things about” – on social media.
What made him think he had even a hope of completing such an epic task? “I was born to do this.” Pedersen had lived in three countries by the age of seven – Denmark, Canada and the US – and spent holidays in a fourth, Finland (his father is Danish, his mother Finnish). “I was uprooted a lot as a child,” he says.
After school and business school, he completed military service and became a UN peacekeeper, stationed in Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti. But he says it was his first overseas logistics job after leaving the army that really shaped him. He went to Libya, then still under Muammar Gaddafi’s rule. “I can barely recognise the person who was sent to Libya and the one who came back,” he says. “I was green, lacking in self-confidence. I came back after two years with proper life experience.”
View image in fullscreen
‘We are far more similar than anyone would ever believe. But we are so quick to see the differences’ … Pedersen in Sri Lanka in 2023.
Photograph: Mike Douglas
He started to work all over the world: in Bangladesh, Greenland, the Arctic Circle, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan, as well as Florida and a number of European countries. He also trained in humanitarian aid and volunteered at a homeless shelter.

data.title: Biff – a batteries-included web framework for Clojure
data.author: TheWiggles
data.article_summary: Biff 是一个包含齐全的 Clojure web 框架，旨在帮助独立开发者快速启动和运行项目，同时避免后续复杂性。它整合了生态系统中的多种工具和库，如 XTDB 数据库（支持不可变性和模式验证）、htmx（用于创建交互式 UI）和无密码认证（通过电子邮件和魔法链接）。Biff 提供 Ubuntu VPS 部署代码和 Docker 支持，便于应用部署。其 REPL 功能允许在保存文件时自动评估更改，支持实时生产环境开发。Biff 文档详尽，默认设置合理但易于修改，适应项目需求变化。

Docs
News
GitHub
Biff helps solo developers move fast.
Get Started
Biff is a batteries-included web framework for Clojure. Launch new projects quickly without getting bogged down in complexity later.
Biff curates libraries and tools from across the ecosystem and composes them into one polished whole.
XTDB
Bring immutability to your database, not just your code. Biff adds schema enforcement with Malli.
htmx
Create rich, interactive UIs without leaving the backend. Throw in a dash of _hyperscript for light client-side scripting.
Authentication
Passwordless, email-based authentication, with support for magic link and one-time passcode flows.
Ready to deploy
Biff comes with code for provisioning an Ubuntu VPS, or you can deploy an Uberjar with Docker.
REPL made easy
Changes are evaluated whenever you save a file. Connect to a production REPL and develop your whole app on the fly.
Meticulously documented
Get started with the tutorial, delve into the reference docs, or tinker with the starter project and inspect the doc strings.
Strong defaults, weakly held.
Biff is designed to be taken apart and modified, so it doesn't get in the way as your needs evolve.

data.title: Cleo, the mathematician that tricked Stack Exchange
data.author: schaum
data.article_summary: Cleo是2013至2015年间活跃于数学问答网站Stack Exchange的一位匿名数学家，因快速准确地解答复杂积分问题而闻名。她提供的答案总是正确，但从不展示中间步骤，引发了数学界对她身份和能力的猜测，有人甚至怀疑她是人工智能。Cleo共回答了39个高难度数学问题，主要涉及复杂积分，且答案通常在几小时内给出。她自称因健康问题无法长时间交流。2025年，Cleo的真实身份揭晓，她是来自乌兹别克斯坦的软件开发员Vladimir Reshetnikov。尽管Cleo的答案正确，但由于缺乏解释，未能符合平台的教育标准，引发了一些争议。

Cleo
was the

from 2013 to 2015, who became known for providing precise answers to complex mathematical
integration
problems without showing any intermediate steps. Due to the extraordinary accuracy and speed of the provided solutions, mathematicians debated whether Cleo was an individual genius, a collective pseudonym, or even an early
artificial intelligence
system.
During the poster's active period, Cleo posted 39 answers to advanced mathematical questions, primarily focusing on complex
integration
problems that had stumped other users. Cleo's answers were characterized by being consistently correct while providing no explanation of methodology, often appearing within hours of the original posts. The account claimed to be limited in interaction due to an unspecified medical condition.

Srinivasa Ramanujan
, known for providing solutions without conventional proofs. In 2025, Cleo was revealed to be
Vladimir Reshetnikov
, a software developer originally from
Uzbekistan
.

data.title: Improving Assembly Code Performance with LLMss via Reinforcement Learning
data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了利用大型语言模型（LLMs）通过强化学习优化汇编代码性能的可能性。作者提出了一种基于Proximal Policy Optimization（PPO）的强化学习框架，通过结合功能正确性和相对于gcc -O3编译器的执行性能的奖励函数来训练LLMs。研究引入了一个包含8,072个真实世界程序的基准，实验结果显示，模型Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-PPO的测试通过率达到96.0%，平均速度比gcc -O3基准快1.47倍，优于包括Claude-3.7-sonnet在内的其他20个模型。这表明强化学习能有效 unlock LLMs 在汇编代码优化方面的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：强化学习在大型语言模型（LLMs）中的应用，特别是在代码优化和性能提升方面的潜力。

不同观点：
• 支持观点：badmonster认为强化学习能够帮助LLMs在汇编级别实现真正的性能优化，而不仅仅局限于生成任务。他引用了具体的数据（1.47x的加速比）来证明其观点，强调这一成果是在gcc -O3优化级别上取得的，而-O3本身已经被高度优化，因此这一成绩具有重要意义。

补充讨论：
• 技术细节：评论中提到了gcc -O3优化级别，表明讨论涉及到编译器优化技术。badmonster的观点隐含了强化学习有可能在传统编译器优化技术上取得进一步突破。
• 争议焦点：目前评论中未见明显反对观点，但潜在争议可能包括强化学习技术在实际应用中的稳定性和可控性，以及其能否在广泛场景下持续超越传统优化方法。

总结：badmonster对强化学习在LLMs中的应用持乐观态度，特别强调了其在代码优化方面的实际效果和潜力，但潜在争议可能涉及其实际应用的广泛性和稳定性。

Title:
Improving Assembly Code Performance with Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Improving Assembly Code Performance with Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning, by Anjiang Wei and 6 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of programming tasks, yet their potential for code optimization remains underexplored. This work investigates whether LLMs can optimize the performance of assembly code, where fine-grained control over execution enables improvements that are difficult to express in high-level languages. We present a reinforcement learning framework that trains LLMs using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), guided by a reward function that considers both functional correctness, validated through test cases, and execution performance relative to the industry-standard compiler gcc -O3. To support this study, we introduce a benchmark of 8,072 real-world programs. Our model, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-PPO, achieves 96.0% test pass rates and an average speedup of 1.47x over the gcc -O3 baseline, outperforming all 20 other models evaluated, including Claude-3.7-sonnet. These results indicate that reinforcement learning can unlock the potential of LLMs to serve as effective optimizers for assembly code performance.

Python Design Patterns

This site is letting me collect my ideas about Python
and Design Patterns all in one place.
My hope is that these pages make the patterns more discoverable —
easier to find in web searches, and easier to read —

The weight of other obligations makes my progress intermittent.
To check for new material,

44037672.article_content:
Imagine you’re watching a highly anticipated video from your favorite YouTube creator — perhaps the moment a famous couple finally gets engaged — when an ad pops up immediately after the clip. This is part of YouTube’s new ad format called “Peak Points.”
The company revealed the new ad format during its Upfront presentation on Wednesday in New York.
Peak Points leverages Google’s Gemini AI to analyze YouTube videos and identify moments it believes have the highest viewer engagement or are most emotionally impactful, and then suggests placing the ad right after it.
Image Credits:
YouTube
Point Peaks aims to benefit advertisers by using a tactic that aims to grab users’ attention right when they’re most invested in the content. This approach appears to be similar to a strategy called
emotion-based targeting
, where advertisers place ads that align with the emotions evoked by the video. It’s believed that when viewers experience heightened emotional states, it leads to better recall of the ads.
However, viewers may find these interruptions frustrating, especially when they’re deeply engaged in the emotional arc of a video and want the ad to be over quickly to resume watching.
In related news, YouTube announced another ad format that may be more appealing to users. The platform debuted a shoppable product feed where users can browse and purchase items during an ad.

The AI industry has promised to “disrupt” large parts of society, and you need look no further than the U.S. educational system to see how effectively it’s done that. Education has been “disrupted,” all right. In fact, the disruption is so broad and so shattering that it’s not clear we’re ever going to have a functional society again.
Probably the most unfortunate and pathetic snapshot of the current chaos being unfurled on higher education is a
recent story by New York magazine
that revealed the depths to which AI has already intellectually addled an entire generation of college students. The story, which involves interviews with a host of current undergraduates, is full of anecdotes like the one that involves Chungin âRoyâ Lee, a transfer to Columbia University who used ChatGPT to write the personal essay that got him through the door:
When he started at Columbia as a sophomore this past September, he didnât worry much about academics or his GPA. âMost assignments in college are not relevant,â he told me. âTheyâre hackable by AI, and I just had no interest in doing them.â While other new students fretted over the universityâs rigorous core curriculum, described by the school as âintellectually expansiveâ and âpersonally transformative,â Lee used AI to breeze through with minimal effort. When I asked him why he had gone through so much trouble to get to an Ivy League university only to off-load all of the learning to a robot, he said, âItâs the best place to meet your co-founder and your wife.â
The cynical view of America’s educational systemâthat it is merely a means by which privileged co-eds can make the right connections, build “social capital,” and get laidâis obviously on full display here. If education isn’t actually about learning anything, and is merely a game for the well-to-do, why not rig that game as quickly, efficiently, and cynically as possible? AI capitalizes on this cynical worldview, exploiting the view-holder and making them stupider while also profiting from them.
When you think about the current assault on the educational system, it’s easy to forget how quickly this has all happened. A more
recent story
from 404 Media shows that the American educational system was largely caught unawares by the deluge of cheating that the AI industry would inspire. After accumulating thousands of pages of school district documents via FOIA requests from around the country, 404’s Jason Koebler found that ChatGPT has “become one of the biggest struggles in American education.” Koebler’s reporting notes that, in the early days of the AI deluge, school districts were courted by “pro-AI consultants” who were known to give presentations that “largely encouraged teachers to use generative AI in their classrooms.” For instance, Koebler writes that the Louisiana Department of Education sent him…
…a presentation it said it consulted called â
ChatGPT and AI in Education
,â made by Holly Clark, the author ofÂ
The AI Infused Classroom
, Ken Shelton, the author ofÂ
The Promises and Perils of AI in Education
, and Matt Miller, the author ofÂ
AI for Educators
. The presentation includes slides that say AI âis like giving a computer a brain so it can learn and make decisions on its own,â note that âitâs time to rethink âplagiarismâ and âcheating,ââ alongside a graph of how students can use AI to help them write essays, â20 ways to use ChatGPT in the classroom,â and â
Warning:
Â Going back to writing essaysâonly in classâcan hurt struggling learners and doesnât get our kids ready for their future.â
In other words, AI acolytes seemed to anticipate that the technology would effectively ruin essay-writing and test-taking, and wanted to spin it to present the ruination as mere “transformation”âa new way of doing thingsâinstead of a destructive force that would devastate education.
This new way of doing things appears to be corrosive not just to students but also to teachers. Koebler’s investigation shows that the AI lobbyists courted schools by making appeals to instructors, showing them that the likes of ChatGPT would make curriculum-building and assignment-giving that much easier. Now, teachers, too, seem to be taking the easy way out, as
a recent New York Times story
shows that college professors have been using chatbots to create their lesson plans, just as their students are using them to complete said lesson.

data.title: Hyper Typing
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了TypeScript类型系统中的一个固有矛盾：更严格的类型更安全，但往往更复杂。作者提出一种称为“过度类型化”（hyper-typing）的现象，即一些库为了追求完美的类型安全，导致类型过于复杂，难以理解，产生难以理解的错误信息，甚至引发不安全的变通方法。作者认为，更简单的类型，甚至是类型生成，通常能带来更实用和愉快的开发体验，尽管它们不那么“完美”。

作者通过一个打印对象属性的函数示例，展示了从宽松类型到严格类型的转变，并指出严格类型提供了编译时的安全保证，但代价是类型定义更加复杂。作者担心“过度类型化”正成为TypeScript生态系统中的趋势，并以TanStack Form库为例，说明这种复杂性如何导致类型文件难以理解、错误信息难以解读，最终迫使开发者使用不安全的变通方法，如将类型强制转换为`any`。

44024173.article_content:
In this article, I talk about an inherent trade-off in TypeScript's type
system: stricter types are safer, but often more complex. I describe a
phenomenon I call "hyper-typing", where libraries - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - end up with overly complex types that are hard-to-understand, produce
cryptic errors, and paradoxically even lead to unsafe workarounds.
I argue that simpler types, or even type generation, often lead to a more
practical and enjoyable developer experience despite being less "perfect".
TypeScript’s type system is
gradual
: when describing a JavaScript value with
TypeScript, you can be more or less accurate, ranging from saying that the value
could be anything (
any
), to describing in absolute detail what the value is
under different conditions.
Consider for example this function which prints the property of an object - if
it exists:
function
printProperty
(
obj
,
key
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
We can type it in a
loose
way as follows:
function
printProperty
(
obj
:
any
,
key
:
string
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
But we can also be more
strict
, requiring
obj
to be an object and
key
to
be one of its properties:
function
printProperty
<
Obj
extends
object
>(
obj
:
Obj
,
key
:
keyof
Obj
)
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
The strictness even allows us to remove the
if
check inside the function,
since now TypeScript gives us the compile-time guarantee that
obj
will always
have property
key
:
//
Passing
in
a
non-existing
property
gives
an
error.
printProperty
({
a:
"a"
},
"b"
);
Argument of type '"b"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"a"'.
Having this additional guarantee is obviously desirable, but it comes at the
expense of making the type definition more complex. Not much in this case - the
type is still very understandable - but it reveals an inherent trade-off. Where
should we draw the line?
Hyper-Typing
Lately I’ve been trying out a few libraries that - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - make their typings so complex that it makes them almost unusable, in my
opinion. I call this approach
hyper-typing
, and I worry it’s becoming a trend
in the TypeScript ecosystem.
I get why, actually. I myself am often a
hyper-typer
! It’s a slippery slope:
“If I add this type constraint then the caller will get an error in this
particular case”. “I can make this function infer this type here so the caller
will get the correct type hint there”.
At the bottom of the slope you get to a place where yes, things work, and they
might also look good for the caller -
in the happy case
. The resulting types,
however, are a complex mess, and the compilation errors produced when the caller
deviates from the happy path are walls of inscrutable text.
An Example: TanStack Form
TanStack Form is the new kid on the block of form libraries. It pushes heavily
on type-safety, promising “first-class TypeScript support with outstanding
autocompletion” for a “smoother development experience”.
What the library accomplishes is honestly impressive. Just give it the default
values of your form and you’re set: now for every form field you define - no
matter how deeply nested - you get the correct type when you read or write its
value, when you do validation, etc.
Don’t look at how the sausage is made, though: you won’t even understand it.
Take
the simple example from TanStack Form’s documentation
.
Use the interactive sandbox and try to check what’s the shape of a field’s
meta
property (or any other library value, really). Here’s what you’ll see:
The
FieldMeta
type has 17 (!) generic parameters and is the intersection of
two types - each taking the same 17 generics - which is where you eventually
find its properties defined.
To be fair, after re-formatting the type definition file and staring at it for a
couple of minutes, I do start to understand what’s going on. For the
FieldMeta
type in particular there’s nothing too obscure, but I can’t help but feel that
this undoubtedly clever and accurate type definition is not actually
helping
me as a user of the library.
Cons of Hyper-Typing
TanStack Form is one example of a hyper-typing library, but as I said, lately
I’ve encountered others that follow a similar approach and leave me with similar
issues:
Badly-formatted type definition files
. This is technically TypeScript’s
fault, but I guess the issue is not apparent until the typings become very
complex. It should be easy to fix, though, just by running the files through
prettier.
Difficult to understand types
. I agree that they’re safer and more
accurate, but that’s not very useful if I don’t understand what they’re
actually describing.
Unsafe workarounds
. Getting into situations where I need to explicitly
define a type is inevitable, and when the library types are so difficult to
understand and use, I often end up resorting to casting things
as any
,
losing

data.title: New research reveals the strongest solar event ever detected, in 12350 BC
data.author: politelemon
data.article_summary: 国际科学家团队利用新开发的SOCOL:14C-Ex模型，确认了公元前12350年发生的最强太阳粒子风暴，这场风暴比公元775年的事件强18%，是此前记录中最强事件的500多倍。该研究扩展了已知太阳活动的强度和时间线，并为分析不同气候条件下的放射性碳变化提供了新方法。这一发现不仅帮助精确定位考古年代，还为评估现代基础设施面对未来太阳风暴的风险提供了“最坏情况”的参考。研究成果发表于《Earth and Planetary Science Letters》。

May 15, 2025
The GIST
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors

the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked

proofread
New research reveals the strongest solar event ever detected, in 12350 BC
by
University of Oulu
Credit:
Earth and Planetary Science Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.epsl.2025.119383
An international team of scientists has discovered an extreme spike in radiocarbon corresponding to the year 12350 BC during the dusk of the last Ice Age. However, the strength of the event could not be assessed earlier because of the lack of an appropriate model. It has now been identified as the most powerful solar particle storm known to date—a colossal space weather storm that struck Earth 14,300 years ago. This recent finding expands the timeline and intensity of known solar activity and sets a new upper boundary for such solar phenomena.
In the study, postdoctoral researcher Kseniia Golubenko and Professor Ilya Usoskin at the University of Oulu, Finland, used their newly developed chemistry–climate model called SOCOL:14C-Ex, specifically designed to reconstruct solar particle storms under ancient glacial climate conditions.
The model confirmed that the detected solar event was approximately 18% stronger than the notorious AD 775 event—until now the strongest solar
storm
ever recorded in tree-ring archives. The work is
published
in the journal
Earth and Planetary Science Letters
.
"Compared to the largest event of the modern satellite era—the 2005 particle storm—the ancient 12350 BC event was over 500 times more intense, according to our estimates," says Dr. Golubenko.
Other large known solar particle storms have occurred around 994 AD, 663 BC, 5259 BC and 7176 BC, and a few other candidates are under investigation. The new model was also verified using wood samples recently found in the French Alps, dating back some 14,300 years.
Solar particle storms are rare, but when they occur, they bombard Earth with an enormous amount of high-energy particles. In comparison, the famous Carrington event in 1859 was a different kind of event and not accompanied by a solar particle storm.
"The ancient event in 12350 BC is the only known extreme solar particle event outside of the Holocene epoch, the past ~12,000 years of stable warm climate," says Golubenko. "Our new model lifts the existing limitation to the Holocene and extends our ability to analyze radiocarbon data even for glacial climate conditions."
In the study, Golubenko and Usoskin designed the SOCOL:14C-Ex model to assess the solar particle storm intensity under glacial conditions. The model was successfully validated using data in tree rings from the AD 775 event and applied to the late Ice Age conditions to study the 12350 BC event.
With the model, the researchers assessed the strength, timing, and terrestrial effects of the most extreme solar particle event presently known. The
model
—now validated under both Holocene and glacial conditions—marks a major step forward in analyzing radiocarbon variations across different climatic and geomagnetic epochs.
The international research team included scientists from France and Switzerland, and was led by Professor Edouard Bard from CEREGE, France.
A new era for radiocarbon dating—and worst-case scenario for solar storms
Solar particle storms can greatly enhance the normal production of cosmogenic isotopes like radiocarbon (
14
C) in the atmosphere by galactic cosmic rays. Such enhanced production, preserved in annual tree rings, serves as a clear cosmic timestamp making possible absolute dating of tree samples.
Such dramatic spikes—known as Miyake events, named after the Japanese researcher who first discovered them—offer invaluable data for scientists studying both
solar activity
, ancient Earth systems and space climate.
"Miyake events allow us to pin down exact calendar years in floating archaeological chronologies," says Usoskin. Radiocarbon signals from such events have already enabled researchers to precisely date Viking settlements in Newfoundland and Neolithic communities in Greece.
The findings revise our understanding of solar physics and space weather extremes. "This event establishes a new
worst-case scenario
," Golubenko notes. "Understanding its scale is critical for evaluating the risks posed by future solar storms to modern infrastructure like satellites, power grids, and communication systems."

data.title: Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning
data.author: mattdesl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个关于神经网络内部表示的假设——"断裂纠缠表示假说"（Fractured Entangled Representation, FER）。作者对比了通过开放式搜索进化而来的神经网络和通过传统随机梯度下降（SGD）训练的网络，在生成单张图像任务中的表现。尽管两者输出结果相似，但内部表示却显著不同。SGD训练的网络展现出一种称为FER的混乱现象，而进化网络则更接近于统一分解表示（UFR）。文章指出，FER可能影响模型的泛化能力、创造力和持续学习能力，因此理解和缓解FER对未来表示学习至关重要。文章还提供了代码和数据可视化，帮助重现研究结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对论文《Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis》的不同看法，尤其是关于AI研究中对模型规模和数据集规模的关注，以及对内部表示的主动修正能力的讨论。

不同观点：
• [mattdesl] 提供了论文的完整标题和链接，似乎只是为了分享资源，没有直接表达个人立场，但隐含了对该论文讨论话题的重视。

• [acc_297] 认为这篇论文很有趣，并且赞同论文中对AI领域过度关注计算规模和数据集规模的批评。他指出，当前很多AI进展过于强调模型的规模和数据量，而在解释模型如何从输入到输出时，常常使用模糊的语言，如流形假设或语义向量。他还特别提到论文中关于人类能够主动重新组织信息的能力与当前大型语言模型（LLMs）缺乏这种能力的比较，认为这是值得注意的。

• [meindnoch] 则认为不应在分享论文标题时加入主观评论，直接指出标题就是“The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis”，似乎在反对[acc_297]的编辑性评论，主张客观呈现论文标题和内容。

补充讨论：
• [acc_297] 提到了论文中的一个关键段落，讨论了人类能够通过重新分析或重新压缩信息来改变内部表示，而不需要额外的输入数据。他认为这一点在当前的LLMs中没有明确的类比，这表明了对AI模型能力局限性的关注。

• [meindnoch] 的评论则提醒讨论应聚焦于论文本身的内容和标题，而不应加入过多的主观解读和评论。

争议焦点：

The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
📝
Paper PDF
Akarsh Kumar
1

2,3

Joel Lehman
4

Kenneth O. Stanley
5

University of British Columbia,
3

4
University of Oxford,
5
Lila Sciences
Abstract
Much of the excitement in modern AI is driven by the observation that scaling up existing systems leads to better performance.
But does better performance necessarily imply better internal representations?
While the representational optimist assumes it must, this position paper challenges that view.
We compare neural networks evolved through an open-ended search process to networks trained via conventional stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on the simple task of generating a single image.
This minimal setup offers a unique advantage: each hidden neuron's full functional behavior can be easily visualized as an image, thus revealing how the network's output behavior is internally constructed neuron by neuron.
The result is striking: while both networks produce the same output behavior, their internal representations differ dramatically.
The SGD-trained networks exhibit a form of disorganization that we term
fractured entangled representation
(FER).
Interestingly, the evolved networks largely lack FER, even approaching a
unified factored representation
(UFR).
In large models, FER may be degrading core model capacities like generalization, creativity, and (continual) learning.
Therefore, understanding and mitigating FER could be critical to the future of representation learning.

Then, set up the python environment with conda:

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

src/fer.ipynb
that quickly covers everything you need.

data.title: Making Video Games (Without an Engine) in 2025
data.author: selvan
data.article_summary: 在2025年，游戏开发者Noel Berry回顾了自己20年的游戏开发经历，强调他并不使用商业游戏引擎如Unity或Unreal，而是通过自建小型工具和系统来开发游戏。Berry认为，不依赖大型“全能”引擎可以更轻松、更有趣，并且能更好地控制开发流程。他主要使用C#语言，并利用现代C#的性能和语法优势，如动态分配栈上数组。他还提到了.NET的热重载功能，使得代码修改可以实时更新，非常适合游戏开发。Berry的开发方式特别适合小型团队，因为C#易于学习和使用，即使是编程新手也能较快上手。他强调，不使用引擎并不意味着从零开始手写所有代码，而是可以借助开源框架和库来实现高效开发。Berry的工作流展示了自定义工具和语言的灵活性，让他能够更自主地进行游戏创作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏引擎开发与使用的权衡，包括自建引擎与使用现成引擎的优劣对比

不同观点：
• **自建引擎的优劣**：
  - **samiv**：认为游戏引擎本身相对简单，真正的难点在于周边工具、内容和资源管线的开发。自建引擎可以更好地满足特定游戏需求，但需要大量工作来支持引擎的运行。
  - **oliverdzedou**：自建引擎虽然前期学习成本高，但一旦掌握，可以节省时间并提供更高的创作自由度。特别是对于独特或小众游戏，自建引擎可能更合适。
  - **z3t4**：从零开始开发项目速度快，且随着开发进展，后续功能实现会更高效。虽然需要多年试错才能掌握合适的架构和抽象，但自建引擎能提供更大控制权。

• **使用现成引擎的优劣**：
  - **danielbarla**：认为使用现成引擎可以避免重复造轮子，特别是在实现复杂功能（如反向动力学和动画混合）时，现成引擎能显著减少开发时间。
  - **leonard-somero**：使用框架处理底层架构，但游戏逻辑和数据操作自己编写，这种方法既能保持对游戏的控制，又不必从头开发引擎。
  - **savory_pancake**、**selvan**：提到开源项目和轻量级引擎（如raylib、Amulet、Love 2D）越来越强大，适合简单游戏开发，且能提供良好的性能和跨平台支持。

• **个人经验与情感**：
  - **noduerme**：怀念Flash时代可以快速编写小型引擎，并混合多种管道进行开发。对当前游戏开发环境感到失望，特别是 indie 游戏在市场上的表现。
  - **thorn**：虽然不开发游戏，但对阅读相关过程感到开心，并从中获得新的视角。

• **成功经验分享**：
  - **trollied**：提到《Celeste》游戏的成功案例，表明自建引擎可以带来商业成功。
  - **Protostome**：询问有经验的开发者如何将游戏开发作为职业，并希望获得建立成功 indie 游戏开发业务的建议。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：自建引擎与使用现成引擎之间的选择主要取决于项目需求和开发者经验。自建引擎提供更多控制和创作自由，但需要大量时间和精力；使用现成引擎则可以加速开发，但可能受限于引擎的通用性和复杂性。
• **工具和架构选择**：开发者对工具和架构的选择多样，从JavaScript、PixiJS到OpenGL、C++等，根据项目需求和个人偏好选择合适的工具链。
• **情感因素**：一些开发者对过去技术（如Flash）的消失感到遗憾，反映出技术变迁对开发者情感的影响。

总结：讨论围绕自建引擎与使用现成引擎的优劣展开，涉及技术细节、个人经验和情感因素，展现了游戏开发社区的多样性和复杂性。

44038209.article_content:
Noel Berry
Making Video Games in 2025 (without an engine)
May 18, 2025
It's 2025 and I am still making video games, which
according to archive.org
is 20 years since I started making games! That's a pretty long time to be doing one thing...
Screenshot of my website circa 2011
When I share stuff I'm working on, people frequently ask how I make games and are often surprised (and sometimes concerned?) when I tell them I don't use commercial game engines. There's an assumption around making games without a big tool like Unity or Unreal that you're out there hand writing your own assembly instruction by instruction.
I genuinely believe making games without a big "do everything" engine can be easier, more fun, and often less overhead. I am not making a "do everything" game and I do not need 90% of the features these engines provide. I am very particular about how my games feel and look, and how I interact with my tools. I often find the default feature implementations in large engines like Unity so lacking I end up writing my own anyway. Eventually, my projects end up being mostly my own tools and systems, and the engine becomes just a vehicle for a nice UI and some rendering...
At which point, why am I using this engine? What is it providing me? Why am I letting a tool potentially destroy my ability to work when they suddenly make
unethical and terrible business decisions
? Or push out an update that they require to run my game on consoles, that also happens to break an entire system in my game, forcing me to rewrite it? Why am I fighting this thing daily for what essentially becomes a glorified asset loader and editor UI framework, by the time I'm done working around their default systems?
The obvious answer for me is to just not use big game engines, and write my own small tools for my specific use cases. It's more fun, and I like controlling my development stack. I know when something goes wrong I can find the problem and address it, instead of submitting a bug report and 3 months later hearing back it "won't be fixed". I like knowing that in another two decades from now I will still be able to compile my game without needing to pirate an ancient version of a broken game engine.
Obviously this is my personal preference - and it's one of someone who has been making indie games for a long time. I used engines like Game Maker for years before transitioning to more lightweight and custom workflows. I also work in very small teams, where it's easy to make one-off tools for team members. But I want to push back that making games "from scratch" is some big impossible task - especially in 2025 with the state of open source frameworks and libraries. A
lot of
popular
indie
games
are made
in small
frameworks like FNA, Love2D, or SDL. Making games "without an engine" doesn't literally mean opening a plain text editor and writing system calls (unless you want to). Often, the overhead of learning how to implement these systems yourself is just as time consuming as learning the proprietary workflows of the engine itself.
With that all said, I think it'd be fun to talk about my workflow, and what I actually use to make games.
Programming Languages
Most of my career I've worked in C#, and aside from a
short stint in C++
a few years ago, I've settled back into a modern C# workflow.
I think sometimes when I mention C# to non-indie game devs their minds jump to what it looked like circa 2003 - a closed source, interpreted, verbose, garbage collected language, and... the language has
greatly
improved since then. The C# of 2025 is vastly different from the C# of even 2015, and many of those changes are geared towards the performance and syntax of the langauge. You can allocate dynamically sized arrays on the stack!
C++
can't do that (
although
C99
can ;) ...
).
The dotnet developers have also implemented hot reload in C# (which works...
most of the time
), and it's pretty fantastic for game development. You can launch your project with
dotnet watch
and it will live-update code changes, which is amazing when you want to change how something draws or the way an enemy updates.
C# also ends up being a great middle-ground between running things fast (which you need for video games) and easy to work with on a day-to-day basis. For example, I have been working on
City of None
with my brother
Liam
, who had done very little coding when we started the project. But over the last year he's slowly picked up the language to the point where he's programming entire boss fights by himself, because C# is just that accessible - and fairly foot-gun free. For small teams where everyone wears many hats, it's a really nice language.
A boss fight that Liam coded
And finally, it has built in reflection... And while I wouldn't use it for release code, being able to quickly reflect on game objects for editor tooling is very nice. I can easily make live-inspection tools that show me the state of game objects without needing any custom meta programming or in-

data.title: Finland announces migration of its rail network to international gauge
data.author: axelfontaine
data.article_summary: 芬兰政府宣布将其铁路网从俄罗斯轨距（1,524毫米）改为欧洲标准轨距（1,435毫米），以加强与欧盟和北约的整合。交通部长Lulu Ranne在赫尔辛基的北欧部长会议上提出了这一历史性决定，旨在提升军事机动性和地区安全，尤其是在芬兰加入北约及与俄罗斯关系紧张的背景下。项目将从北部奥卢附近开始，消除芬兰与瑞典、挪威之间运输部队和物资的技术障碍。政府预计在2027年7月做出最终决定，2032年左右开始建设，欧盟资金将是关键，可能覆盖高达50%的规划费用和30%的建设费用。这一耗资数十亿欧元、影响超过9,200公里轨道、历时数十年的转变，标志着芬兰在地缘政治和战略上的重大转变。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：芬兰及欧洲铁路轨距转换项目的可行性、成本、战略意义及技术实施。

不同观点：
• vesinisa：认为目前的宣布只是政治姿态，缺乏具体的技术计划。对成本和实际执行持怀疑态度，预测项目可能永远不会真正开始建设。
• dewey：引用WSJ视频，强调该项目的地缘政治意义，尤其是对北约和俄罗斯的影响。
• gorgoiler：对项目持乐观态度，认为已有技术如道砟清洁机可以有效用于轨道更新，并设想更大规模的设备应用。
• blueflow：提供开放铁路地图链接，让读者查看具体轨道拓扑。
• radicalbyte：认为这是战略举措，有助于在欧洲内部移动武器，并阻碍俄罗斯入侵时的后勤。建议在整个欧洲推广。
• Yizahi：支持该项目，强调对防御俄罗斯的重要性，并引用乌克兰战争中的铁路物流实例。
• thih9：对项目实施方式提出疑问，询问是否会有两套系统并行或在特定区域更新轨道，并寻求其他国家的类似案例。
• apexalpha：认为项目成本高昂，但因为俄罗斯轨距较宽，情况还算有利。期望在乌克兰等地的未来项目中应用经验。
• indiantinker：质疑项目的成本效益，以西班牙为例，指出不同轨距共存的可行性，并建议更多支持小企业和自由职业者创新。
• Havoc：怀疑项目与北约军事物资快速运输的需求有关。
• mikewarot：认为转换轨距应是相对简单的过程，引用美国过去的经验，质疑项目为何需多年努力。
• helsinkiandrew：提供更深入的背景文章链接。
• varsketiz：作为邻近俄罗斯的国家居民，希望自己国家也进行类似项目。
• cromulent：指出该提案来自欧盟委员会，芬兰最初因费用问题反对。
• ggm：支持项目，认为可以改善铁路的弯道、双轨和坡度，带来多方面的好处。

补充讨论：
- 项目的地缘政治和战略意义是讨论的核心，尤其是对俄罗斯和北约的影响。
- 技术实施细节和成本估算存在争议，部分评论者对项目的可行性和必要性表示怀疑。
- 不同国家如西班牙的轨距共存经验被作为参考，提出其他可能的解决方案。
- 对欧盟资金使用和项目优先级的质疑，以及对小企业和自由职业者创新支持的呼吁。

44038835.article_content:
Finnish VR Sm3 series Pendolino unit in Helsinki (CC BY SA) FALK2-Wikimedia Commons. Image cropped.
The Finnish government has announced the conversion of its rail network from Russian gauge (1,524 mm) to European standard (1,435 mm). This historic decision reinforces its integration with the European Union and NATO.
The change, presented by Transport Minister Lulu Ranne at a meeting of Nordic ministers in Helsinki, is in response to the need to improve military mobility and regional security, especially in the wake of Finland’s NATO membership and growing tensions with Russia.
The project, which will start in the north of the country near Oulu, aims to remove technical obstacles to transporting troops and goods between Finland, Sweden and Norway.
The government is expected to make the final decision by July 2027, with construction starting around 2032. European funding will be key: the EU could cover up to 50% of planning costs and 30% of construction
.
The transition, which will cost billions of euros, affect more than 9,200 km of track, and take decades, symbolises a geopolitical and strategic shift for Finland, which, with this decision, fully aligns itself with European infrastructure.

data.title: The Entropy of Thought: Why Our Minds Gravitate Toward Divided Realities
data.author: victorasao
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人类信念的形成和演变，提出信念从我们感知世界的方式开始，通过与外部刺激（如人、气味、文字等）的情感关联而逐渐构建。这些情感关联存储在一个无意识的“图书馆”中，最强烈和最早的记忆离我们更近。随着年龄增长，重遇这些刺激会引发新的情感反应，形成不断更新的情感平均值。物理实体倾向于分散，而数字实体则趋于聚集，这种物理与数字模式的不同演化受到熵的原理影响。文章还介绍了adiem.com正在开发的一个利用AI观察心率模式的应用，旨在解决社交焦虑和ADHD等问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：心灵、情绪、外部刺激与数字实体的关系，及其对社会问题和心理健康的影响

不同观点：
• [victorasao] 认为，人类的心智会将情绪与外部刺激关联起来，并随着时间推移形成信念集群。他通过将热力学熵与信息理论进行类比，提出物理实体倾向于分散，而数字实体则倾向于聚集，导致现实的分裂。这种视角有助于理解数字时代中的社交焦虑和ADHD等问题。

• [ImHereToVote] 则指出，生物神经网络本身不能成为真理机器，默认情况下无法寻求真理。他认为，只有文化才能塑造寻求真理的行为。

补充讨论：
• [victorasao] 的观点中包含了对信息组织和心理健康问题的跨学科思考，特别是数字实体集群如何影响人们的认知和情绪状态。
• [ImHereToVote] 的评论则聚焦于生物神经网络的局限性，强调文化在塑造人类认知行为中的关键作用。
• 争议焦点可能在于，数字实体集群是否必然导致现实的分裂，以及生物神经网络是否具备潜在的真理寻求能力，还是完全依赖于文化影响。

44038812.article_content:
Why Ideas Cluster and People Disperse
When Patterns Collide: Why Your Matter and Digital Life Are Spiralling Differently
Victor Anastasiu
Follow
3 min read
·
Feb 13, 2025
--
Listen
Share
Beliefs are, in many ways, what define each of us from a mental perspective.
No two people in the world share the exact same belief system. These beliefs can range from something as simple as “egg whites are better than yolks” to deeply philosophical or theological questions like “Does God have a beard?”
The structure of a belief is highly sophisticated. I suspect it starts with how we perceive the world from the moment we exist as mere cells — perhaps even earlier, embedded in our DNA. However, I want to focus on the stage where we become individuals, holistic beings with minds capable of self-reflection.
The short version of my hypothesis is this: At some point in our development, we begin experiencing pleasure and pain in various forms, with an infinite spectrum of emotions in between. These sensations always occur in conjunction with external stimuli — people, scents, words, locations, sounds, and so on.
Since our minds are finely tuned pattern-recognition machines, they associate these complex internal emotions with the external stimuli present at that moment. Everything around us in that experience gets grouped together and labeled with the specific emotion we felt at the time.
Let’s call this
Emotion X1
, where X varies, representing the full scale emotions from infinite pain to infinite pleasure.
These associations are then stored in a vast, unconscious
library
— a spherical one, with
ourselves at its center
. The most intense and oldest emotional memories are closer to us, while the rest extend outward, scattered across infinite distances.
As we age and re-encounter familiar stimuli — whether people, words, or places — our past emotional associations resurface. However, they now appear in
slightly altered configurations
, leading to new emotional responses, which we’ll call
Emotion X2
.
Simplistically, our minds label everything in that experience with X2. Some elements will be newly labeled, while others already had the X1 label. When this happens, the new emotional label becomes an
average
of the previous and current experiences:
(X1 + X2) / 2
As we continue through life, every external pattern we encounter accumulates emotional weight, forming a running average:
(X1 + X2 + … + Xn) / n
The more a belief is reinforced by positive emotions the more it moved closer to us within the metaphorical, spherical library. In a feedback loop they become more salient to us or the first choice of lenses we use to “see” the world.
This applies not only to
physical
patterns — like people, foods, or objects — but also to
digital
entities, such as
words or ideas
.
But here’s where things get interesting and challenging.
Why, because it is good to associate pain with fingers in fire but when you associate pain with a non physical entity, like the word or image of fire, things get strange.
The Key Difference Between Physical and Digital Entities
There’s a fundamental difference between how
physical
and
digital
patterns evolve in our minds:
Physical entities tend to disperse.
Digital entities tend to cluster.
In physics, this is measured by
entropy
— a principle stating that physical systems naturally move toward disorder.
Recent studies support these fundamentally different observations:
Entropy in physical systems increases
(Thermodynamic Law).
Entropy in digital systems decreases
(
Infodynamics Law)
.
As humans, we are bound to balance these two colliding entropies in a process we name life.
Following these observations, at
adiem.com
, we build an
Apple-watch wearable app
and a platform that is leveraging the power of AI to observe how certain heartbeat patters evolve over time in both individual and collective setup.
While this might look as the future for adiem the present is educating and addressing more urgent needs like social anxiety and ADHD both human reactions when dealing with unbalanced entropy.
We named this space the intelligence of rhythm and one very interesting framework we resonate with is brilliantly exposed here by our friend
Benjamin James
in
his research
.

主要讨论点：AI在科学研究中的应用及其潜在问题，包括 survivorship bias（幸存者偏差）以及AI方法与传统方法的比较。

不同观点：
• CGMthrowaway认为，AI在科学研究中的应用导致并加剧了幸存者偏差问题。由于AI研究人员很少发表负面结果，导致大量未发表的失败实验或无效结果，使得科学研究的可信度受到影响。他还指出，在AI广泛应用之前，已经有85-90%的研究结果未被发表，AI可能会进一步加剧这一问题。

• acc_297没有直接表达立场，但提供了一个相关讨论的链接，暗示可能有其他讨论或资源对当前话题有补充或对比作用，引导读者参考另一篇文章以获得更全面的视角。

• staunton对AI在科学问题中的实际效果提出质疑。他认为该论文中使用的神经网络方法只是解决了一些高中水平的简单问题，而这些问题完全可以通过传统的数值求解器更便宜地解决。因此，他怀疑使用神经网络只是为了追随潮流，而不是因为其在解决特定问题时具有实际优势。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是AI在科学研究中是否真正提供了超越传统方法的优势。staunton的观点表明，在某些情况下，AI可能并非最佳选择，而只是因为流行而被使用。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是幸存者偏差问题，特别是在AI研究中，负面结果的发表不足可能会影响整个领域的进展和可信度。
- 不同评论者对AI在科学中的实际价值和应用场景存在不同看法，这反映了对新兴技术在传统领域应用效果的广泛讨论和争议。

data.title: Mary Queen of Scots Channel Anamorphosis, a 3D Simulation
data.author: nih
data.article_summary: 作者在研究其在线书籍《The Lost Art of Logarithms》时，深入探讨了对数的历史及其文化、政治和宗教背景，特别关注约翰·纳皮尔在1593年出版的《启示录》数学分析及其与1588年西班牙无敌舰队入侵英格兰企图推翻伊丽莎白女王事件的关联。作者还研究了苏格兰玛丽女王的相关历史，并发现了一幅名为《玛丽，苏格兰女王》的变形画作。该画作通过三棱镜效果展示，从不同角度看分别呈现女性面孔和骷髅。作者通过WebGL技术模拟了3D效果，并提供了图像分离和合并的编程过程，最终实现了动态展示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术家在作品中放置头骨位置的选择

不同观点：
• **观点一**（ljsprague）：质疑艺术家为何不将头骨放在与头部相同的位置。这个评论者对作品的构图提出疑问，认为头骨和头部的对齐可能是更合理的安排，可能在寻求艺术构图上的逻辑或象征意义。

• **观点二**（artenthusiast22）：头骨的位置可能象征着死亡或生命的脆弱，并不一定需要与头部位置对齐。他们认为艺术作品中的元素安排可以超越现实的物理逻辑，更多的是传达情感或概念。

• **观点三**（visualcritic123）：提出头骨的偏离位置可能是为了创造视觉上的不平衡，从而引发观者的不安或思考。这种刻意的错位可能是艺术家用来挑战观众对生命与死亡的常规理解。

补充讨论：
• **关于象征意义的讨论**：有评论提到头骨在艺术史中常被用来象征死亡，而其位置的偏离可能象征着现代人与死亡之间的心理距离。

• **关于艺术自由的讨论**：部分评论指出，艺术创作具有主观性，不应过度解读或限制艺术家的表达方式，头骨位置的选择可能是艺术家个人风格或情感的体现。

• **争议焦点**：头骨位置的安排是否需要遵循现实逻辑，或者是否可以完全基于艺术家的创作自由。部分评论者认为艺术作品应有一定逻辑，而另一些评论者则强调艺术不应被束缚于现实规则。

44016059.article_content:
Iâve been going down some odd rabbit holes recently while researching my free online book-in-progress
The Lost Art of Logarithms
. Although the book is mostly focused on the history, use, meaning, and importance of logarithms, I believe that even histories of science and mathematics profit by being placed within political, cultural, social, and religious contexts.
This is particularly true of John Napierâs invention of logarithms. It seems that Napier began thinking about logarithmic concepts while working on his first book â a mathematical analysis of the Book of Revelation published in 1593. Although Napier had been working on this book for some years, it was given special urgency by the attempted invasion of England by the Spanish Armada in 1588, which had as its goal the overthrow of Queen Elizabeth. Spain decided to launch this attack by the shift in European geopolitics following the 1587 execution of Mary Queen of Scots.
I have therefore been deep into research into the Protestant Reformation in general, the English and Scottish Reformations in particular, and the major players within these movements, including the Tudors and the Stuarts. While reading about Mary Queen of Scots, I came upon a reference to a channel anamorphosis painting (also known as a
turning picture
or a
tabula scalata
) on display in the National Portrait Gallery in Edinburgh, so of course I immediately thought about creating a 3D simulation.
Hereâs a short (15-second) YouTube video of a progressive view of the painting as the viewer moves from left to right:
The image shifts from a womanâs face to a skull.
The National Galleries website labels this painting as
Anamorphosis, called Mary, Queen of Scots
, the word âcalledâ suggesting that it might not actually be her. The artist is unknown but the date of composition is given as 1580, which is several years before Mary was executed, so the transformation into a skull seems a little premature.
The two images are painted on a panel built from a row of prisms, which Iâve mimicked here with 3D graphics using WebGL:
You can drag this image with your mouse or your finger to view the prismed panel from different directions. I found an article entitled
"The Mathematics of the Channel Anamorphosis"
that concluded that the prisms in the Mary Queen of Scots painting used angles of 45Â°, 45Â°, and 90Â°, and thatâs how I constructed the panel.
The National Galleries website allows downloading and using two images of the painting with a âpersonal-use license agreementâ that permits its use âon websites that are primarily information led, research oriented and non-commercial.â I will be using these images in an educational manner in this blog entry to demonstrate how they can be turned into a 3D simulation.
The two images on the National Galleries website show the painting from two different perspectives:
Alas, each of these two perspectives shows about 2/3rd of one image and about 1/3rd of the other.
From each of these bitmaps I had to extract images that were mostly one and not the other. I measured pixel positions manually and then wrote a little WPF program in C# to construct better separated images:
This is far from perfect, but I didnât expect something immaculate.
The next step was to merge the two images by alterating the strips:
This looks peculiar, of course, but now itâs ready to be overlaid on the 3D prism panel. And hereâs the result:
Swipe the image with your mouse (with button pressed) or finger from right to left to turn the face into a skull.
All the JavaScript source code for rendering the 3D image is attached to this HTML file. I apologize for the plethora of files; they are part of an infrastructure to allow me to use WebGL in a reasonbly straightforward manner.

data.title: Mecha: Portable Linux Computing
data.author: handfuloflight
data.article_summary: Mecha Systems提供硬件和软件支持，旨在打造无限制的计算平台。其核心产品Mecha Comet是一款便携式可编程Linux计算机，专注于边缘计算和扩展性。硬件设计可3D打印，并支持云服务快速连接。软件方面，Mecha致力于开源项目，包括Mechanix Shell、Rust Cloud Agent和MCTK用户界面框架等。公司注重可持续发展，采用可回收材料，设计易于维修，并提供十年系统支持。Mecha还设有Pilot计划，支持开源项目开发，并定期参加技术交流活动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对网络甲板（cyberdeck）项目的技术细节和实际应用情况的评价与期望

不同观点：
• ValdikSS认为当前所有的网络甲板项目都使用了功耗较高的系统级芯片（SoCs），即使在屏幕关闭的情况下，其功耗也在1W以上。这对他来说是个很大的缺点，影响了他对这类项目的兴趣。

• notorandit表示对RISC-V处理器的期望，认为如果这些项目能够采用RISC-V CPU会更有吸引力，但同时也承认这些项目的想法本身非常有趣。

• ktallett则关注实际设备的实现和功能展示，询问是否已经有建成的设备和实际运行的例子，显示出对项目实际成果的关注。

补充讨论：
- ValdikSS关注的是设备的功耗问题，特别是SoCs在空闲状态下的电力消耗，这反映了对便携设备续航能力的重视。
- notorandit的评论则涉及到对处理器架构的偏好，尤其是对开源架构RISC-V的兴趣，指向了技术选择的讨论。
- ktallett的提问揭示了对项目实际进展和可行性的关注，暗示了对概念验证或实际例证的需求。

争议焦点：
- 主要争议点在于这些项目在实际应用中的可行性和功耗问题。ValdikSS对高功耗的批评与其他用户对项目创意和潜在技术选择的兴趣形成了对比。
- 另一个潜在的争议是对不同处理器架构的偏好，如notorandit对RISC-V的期待与其他用户未提及具体架构需求之间的差异。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某个人针对AI提出的极端主张及其背景的讨论

不同观点：
• [brap] 认为该人作为记者的背景让人质疑其提出关于AI的极端主张的资格。言下之意是该人缺乏足够的技术或专业知识来支撑其观点。
• [hengheng] 指出该人可能会提倡极端行动（如“摧毁管道”），但自己并不会付诸实践。这种行为模式曾在其他场合见过，暗示对这种言行不一致的怀疑。
• [flave] 认为这种极端立场是一种策略，可能是从气候变化倡导团体借鉴而来，旨在通过极端立场来“转移可接受言论的范围”。然而，flave认为这种策略是不道德、危险且自 defeating（自我挫败）的。具体来说，不道德是因为欺骗性行为本身有问题；危险是因为会吸引神经质、精神不稳定或被误导的狂热追随者；自我挫败是因为会让那些有一定理解但不深入的人对该立场产生反感，而这些人往往掌握着重要的权力和资源。
• [KaiserPro] 认为这种极端反AI发展的观点并不新颖，且对其能实现的目标表示怀疑。KaiserPro指出，即使在某个地区限制AI发展，开发活动也可能转移到其他地方。此外，KaiserPro提到AI带来的风险更可能是社会动荡（如失业引发的民怨），而非AI直接伤害人类。
• [fnands] 质疑创建一个名为“AI安全中心”的非营利组织并在Twitter上发布极端言论的价值，暗示这种行为可能只是为了吸引注意力，而非真正推进有意义的讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该人提出的极端主张是否合理、可行及其背后的动机。
• 讨论还涉及到这种极端策略是否道德、危险以及是否会适得其反。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对AI发展潜在风险的不同看法，特别是关于AI对社会的影响是通过直接技术风险还是社会问题（如失业）产生的。

data.title: Russia's Pravda Network: AI-Driven Disinformation on a Global Scale
data.author: haizhung
data.article_summary:
文章总结了俄罗斯相关的广泛虚假信息网络“Pravda”和“Portal Kombat”，它们通过数百个伪装成当地新闻网站的平台传播亲克里姆林宫内容，影响全球舆论。自2022年起，该网络发布了超过370万篇文章，尤其针对欧洲和亚洲国家，如法国、德国、乌克兰等。其策略包括大规模复制和放大来自俄罗斯官方媒体的内容，通过自动化翻译软件传播，旨在增强亲俄观点，削弱国际对乌克兰的支持，破坏民主政府信任。

该网络对政治、安全和AI发展构成重大风险，尤其在信息污染和开放源情报（OSINT）收集方面。其高频虚假信息可能污染用于训练大型语言模型（LLM）的数据集，甚至影响维基百科等平台，进而误导公众和AI系统。该网络的去中心化结构使其难以彻底清除，对全球信息完整性和AI安全形成长期挑战。

Russia’s Pravda Network: AI-Driven Disinformation on a Global Scale
Europe
Diplomacy and Security
Technology
14 May
Written By
Analyst
Mejreme Asllani
| 14 May 2025
Summary
A widespread Russian-linked network, 'Pravda' and 'Portal Kombat' operates hundreds of websites globally, mimicking local news outlets to amplify pro-Kremlin narratives.
This network generates significant political and security risks by disseminating disinformation and potentially compromising open-source intelligence (OSINT) gathering and Artificial Intelligence (AI) training datasets.
The network will likely persist and increasingly leverage AI, evolving into more sophisticated automated Information Operations (IO) tactics that will likely challenge global information integrity and AI safety in the long term.
The global information space serves as a critical battleground where state-affiliated entities employ increasingly sophisticated methods to influence perceptions and advance geopolitical agendas. A notable example is the extensive pro-Kremlin disinformation network identified by the
Atlantic Council’s Digital Forensic Research Lab
(DFRLab),
CheckFirst
and the French digital vigilance agency,
VIGINUM
. Named
'Pravda'
by DFRLab due to its domain naming conventions (e.g.,
pravda-fr.com
,
pravda-de.com
,
serbia.news-pravda.com
), the network also includes a particularly large and coordinated subset referred to as
'Portal Kombat'
.
This operation has been active since at least
early 2022
, disseminating content regarding the war in Ukraine, witha significant worldwide increase in 2024. The Pravda ecosystem encompasses hundreds of news websites with over
3.7m
published articles, meticulously designed to mimic the content of legitimate local news portals across Europe, the Americas, and Asia. Key European countries targeted by the Pravda network include
France, Germany, Ukraine, Moldova and Serbia
.
The primary strategy of networking avoids original content creation. Instead, it focuses on the large-scale copy-paste and amplification of
narratives favourable to the Kremlin
. This content is often taken directly from
Russian state media outlets
like Sputnik, RT,
RIA, Telegram,
official government statements, social media posts by Russian politicians, and pro-Kremlin supporters, and translated into the local language utilising
automatic translation
software. The network operates by flooding the digital sphere with high volumes of repetitive content through digital automation and
almost to human generation
. The overall aim of this network is multifaceted: to increase pro-Kremlin viewpoints in foreign information ecosystems, exacerbate existing societal divisions, undermine international support for Ukraine, erode public trust in democratic governments and credible media institutions, and ultimately shape a global narrative more aligned with
Russia's strategic goals
.
The Pravda/Portal Kombat network carries profound implications across political, operational, security, and potentially economic domains. Politically, it constitutes a persistent, low-cost tool for foreign interference, aiming to subtly manipulate public discourse, disseminate pro-Russia, anti-Ukraine, and anti-NATO narratives and potentially sway opinions on critical foreign policy decisions or during election cycles within targeted countries. Moreover, the network operates against nations imposing sanctions on Russia, effectively undermining these restrictions by disseminating targeted content. Its tactics also challenge national sovereignty by attempting to circumvent domestic media regulations and directly influence citizens.
Operationally, the network's decentralised structure and reliance on easily replicable website templates make it highly resilient. Exposing and dismantling one cluster often proves insufficient, as new domains can be quickly established, demonstrating an adaptability that complicates takedown efforts. This presents a persistent challenge for content moderators and cybersecurity agencies. The most significant security risk lies in the deliberate pollution of the information environment on an overwhelming scale. The sheer volume of content makes discerning credible information more difficult for the average user and complicates OSINT gathering for analysts. Critically, this flood of disinformation risks contaminating the vast datasets used to train
Large Language Models (LLMs)
and other
AI systems
. This concerns especially
manipulation of Wikipedia content
by Pravda network,  as these LLMs are considered to get primary sources of knowledge from Wikipedia. The documented operation of Pravda-network content being cited on platforms like Wikipedia or ingested by AI tools illustrates a dangerous pathway for
disinformation laundering
, where biased or false narratives can be absorbed and presented as neutral facts by systems trusted and used by millions of people.

data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hetzner服务器的可靠性、价格和适用性

不同观点：
• adamcharnock认为Hetzner的专用服务器非常稳定，尤其是通过设计冗余和多可用区等策略后，表现优异。尽管存在偶尔的计划外路由器停机问题，但整体性价比仍然高于AWS。
• jeduardo基于六年前的体验，认为Hetzner的服务器不可靠，类似于EC2 Spot实例，随时可能下线，且数据容易丢失。他建议在有足够预算时迁移到更可靠的提供商。
• herbst从个人使用廉价服务器的角度出发，指出Hetzner的网络不可靠，支持也不够好，只适合非关键任务的背景任务。
• danielops提到在过去一年中Hetzner的可靠性显著下降，尤其是Storage Boxes的多次长时间不可用问题，且状态页面没有及时更新。
• jesterson认为所有服务提供商都会在状态页面上有所隐瞒，只有大规模或不可忽视的故障才会被反映出来。Hetzner的价格低廉，适合某些业务需求，但不适合对可靠性要求极高的用户。
• preisschild的经验较为正面，表示在使用Hetzner云机器时没有遇到类似问题，只有常规的服务器停机和故障报告通知。

补充讨论：
• Hetzner的服务在不同用户之间的体验差异较大，部分用户如adamcharnock和preisschild有良好的体验，而danielops和jeduardo则遇到了较多的问题。
• 争议的焦点在于Hetzner的可靠性和性价比之间的平衡。部分用户认为其低价策略牺牲了可靠性，而另一些用户则通过设计冗余系统来弥补这一不足。
• 对于Hetzner状态页面更新不及时的问题，jesterson指出这是行业普遍现象，而非Hetzner独有。
• 一些用户如danielops对Hetzner的支持和透明度表示不满，认为在问题发生时缺乏及时的沟通和解决方案。
• 总体而言，用户对Hetzner的评价呈现出两极分化的态势，有些用户对其表现感到满意，而另一些用户则因遇到的问题而感到失望。

data.title: Hasbro, the custodians of D&D, have no idea what to do with BG3's success
data.author: AntiRush
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了《龙与地下城》(Dungeons & Dragons, D&D)品牌在Hasbro及其子公司Wizards of the Coast (WoTC)管理下的困境。尽管《博德之门3》(Baldur's Gate 3)取得了巨大成功，被誉为CRPG的巅峰之作，但Hasbro在其管理上却屡屡失误。文章提到，Larian Studios精心打造了《博德之门3》这一“金蛋”，但随后Hasbro却大幅裁员，可能影响未来与Larian的合作。此外，WoTC推出的虚拟桌面游戏Sigil也因管理不善而面临失败。Hasbro对D&D的未来发展方向不明，令玩家和业内人士担忧。文章批评Hasbro的短视决策，并质疑其能否妥善利用《博德之门3》的成功。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44038512.article_content:
(Image credit: Wizards of the Coast (via GamesRadar).)
Dungeons & Dragons might be, if trends continue, one of the most mishandled success stories I've ever seen. And, if my powers of prophecy are correct, we're starting to approach the low bend of a 10+ year arc where Hasbro, the parent company of D&D owners Wizards of the Coast (WoTC), has continually fumbled the bag in just about every way it possibly could.
Usually when I hammer out a timeline like this, I work in chronological order—but we're going to start in media res. It'll actually help us to work backwards: Starting with Baldur's Gate 3.
In case you hadn't heard, we rather like Baldur's Gate 3 here at PC Gamer. While not all of us are CRPG-heads, those of us that
are
would probably consider it one of the all-time greats. Our own Fraser Brown even called it "the pinnacle of the genre" in his
Baldur's Gate 3 review
.
You may like
'Hasbro pushed Sigil out of the nest': D&D's latest layoffs happened because the 'distinct monetization path' for its virtual tabletop Sigil never materialized
It's not looking good for D&D's virtual tabletop Sigil, as Hasbro follows a quiet release by reportedly laying off 90% of the people working on it
Baldur's Gate 3 and Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 show that the future of RPGs is in games way more ambitious, weird and unexpected than anything Bethesda and BioWare have to offer
For Hasbro and WoTC, it was the savviest deal possible for the "world's greatest role-playing game"—grabbing one of the best RPG development studios of our time to make something so far up its alley, it's like it was born for the job. Larian Studios, a shining goose to end all geese, spent several years meticulously creating a golden egg.
Except in this metaphor, the goose has now waddled off, leaving Hasbro to run around carrying its egg-treasure with a brow full of flop-sweat—wide, panicked eyes looking for a place to actually put it. Their first move?
Lay off most of the people
who got Larian to make the thing in the first place. Yeah, I don't know either.
The goose has now waddled off, leaving Hasbro to run around carrying its egg-treasure with a brow full of flop-sweat."
I want to be clear: The idea that Larian decided not to make another Baldur's Gate game because of these layoffs is pure conjecture, and countermand to
Swen Vincke's words on the subject
. It's clear that the developer simply wanted to move onto games it was more passionate about, lest it consign itself to the geese farm forevermore.
Not to mention, there's plenty of reasons why you might want to make your own IP rather than continuing to pay dividends to another company—BioWare did something very similar, hopping from Knights of the Old Republic to Mass Effect back in the day.

Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
But, like, Hasbro can't have
helped,
right? As a studio, Larian's
extremely outspoken
about the kind of cost-cutting, short-sighted nonsense it pulled. Bare minimum, it would've been a point in the 'cons' column. Still, as Vincke has demanded—my tinfoil hat is off. The point is, Hasbro won't get another D&D game out of Larian. So what now?
Sigil's a bad sign
A huge amount of TTRPG players have, due to the struggles that come with trying to organise five adults into the same room every week, turned to Virtual Tabletops (VTTs) to get their fix. I'm one of them: Most of my games are online.
(Image credit: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond)
WoTC decided to muscle in on the territory itself with Sigil—its own glossy VTT, a one-stop shop for all your D&D fun. Sensibly, Hasbro decided to put
Baldur's Gate 3's cast in it as minis
—which, while kinda kitschy, is in itself pretty cute. There's some table that'd get a kick out of Astarion guest-starring in their campaign, I'm sure.
Except Sigil's not going to be the next big thing, and it might barely be a 'thing' at all. Sigil went into playtesting with a whimper, didn't quite work, and then Hasbro had 90% of the people making it
laid off
because,
reportedly
, "Hasbro treated Sigil like a video game instead of a VTT and at no point cared to understand the difference."
So what's Hasbro doing with Baldur's Gate 3?
The answer is an uncertain 'er'.
Certainly, the line is that they've got exciting news to share just around the corner (who doesn't) but just listen to senior vice president of Digital Strategy and Licensing at Hasbro, Eugene Evans, as he spoke to PCG's own Robin Valentine last year:
"I think it's too early to express specifics and I think that there's a much bigger question about how we approach Baldur's Gate in the future … But I would like to think that all of those characters, for the sake of the fans, could potentially appear in future products."
