data.title: The Dawn of Nvidia's Technology
data.author: wmf
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Nvidia崛起背后的关键技术和商业决策，以及两本介绍该公司及其创始人黄仁勋的书。作者以内部人的视角，回顾了Nvidia早期的创新，包括成像模型和I/O架构。在成像模型方面，Nvidia最初采用 quadric patches 技术，以更少的数据实现更真实的3D图像，这在与Sega合作时取得成功。然而，随着微软推出DirectX，坚持使用quadric patches 可能导致失败，因为开发者需要适应基于三角形的图形标准。在I/O架构上，Nvidia的虚拟化对象设计和资源管理器使其芯片能够更快迭代，成为长期优势。文章还提到在Sun Microsystems的经历，强调开放源代码和及时决策的重要性。作者对两本书的商业描述部分给予肯定，但对技术细节的解读提出质疑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图形硬件发展的历史、技术细节及其影响

不同观点：
• Animats认为，早期的CPU与图形设备之间的交互缺乏标准化，导致各种设计选择（如三角形或四边形、共享内存或命令队列等）。虽然Vulkan在一定程度上标准化了这些交互，但仍暴露了许多硬件设计决策，使得不同硬件有不同的选项和性能权衡。相比之下，OpenGL隐藏了这些细节，因此仍被广泛使用。
• mrandish赞赏对历史技术发展的回顾，认为这些第一手资料有助于理解技术演变过程，并为未来的技术决策提供参考。特别强调了经过几十年后的反思，更能看清关键决策的结果。
• jacobgorm分享了与NVIDIA员工的个人经历，提到NVIDIA在硬件模块化方面的创新，以及未实现的Amiga硬件授权计划，认为这是技术和商业决策的结果。
• cadamsdotcom引用了Kim和Michael Hara的观点，强调了灵活设计（软件与硬件结合）在技术开发中的重要性，使得产品能够在错过功能或截止日期时仍能成功。
• pjmlp分享了个人的硬件购买经历，从Voodoo卡换到Riva TNT，反映出当时硬件兼容性问题对消费者的影响。
• artyom将NVIDIA的故事与其他工程奇迹（如Bell Labs、Xerox）相比较，认为这些成就源于 clever工程师的自由时间和无干扰的管理环境。
• killme2008对图形编程推动面向对象编程的广泛应用表示赞赏，认为设备抽象在技术上下文中非常优雅。
• trinsic2对Nvidia及其CEO Jensen Huang的成功持怀疑态度，认为Nvidia通过市场强势地位对合作伙伴施压，表现得像其他掠夺性企业一样。

补充讨论：
• tiahura提供了与早期Nvidia卡相关的演讲链接，为讨论提供了额外的技术背景资料。
• rjsw提到自己仍保留着NV1卡，反映了早期图形硬件的收藏价值。
• 2OEH8eoCRo0指出文中未提及SGI，暗示对SGI在图形硬件历史中的贡献未被重视。

争议焦点：
• Nvidia的成功是否完全归功于其技术创新，还是更多地依赖于市场运作和商业策略。Trinsic2对Jensen Huang和Nvidia的批评与其他对技术创新的赞赏形成对比。

44043687.article_content:
Because
Nvidia
became one of the most valuable companies in the world, there are now two books explaining its rise and extolling the genius of Jensen Huang, Tae Kim's
The Nvidia Way: Jensen Huang and the making of a tech giant
, and Steven Witt's
The Thinking Machine: Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and the World's Most Coveted Microchip
. For the later 90% of the history I wasn't there, so I won't comment on their treatment of that part. But for the pre-history at
Sun Microsystems
and the first 10% of the history I was there. Kim's account of the business side of this era is detailed and, although it was three decades ago, matches my recollections.
Witt's account of the business side of the early history is much less detailed and some of the details don't match what I remember.
But as regards the technical aspects of this early history it appears that neither author really understood the reasons for the two kinds of innovation we made; the imaging model and the I/O architecture. Witt
writes (Page 31)
:
The first time I asked Priem about the architecture of the NV1, he spoke uninterrupted for twenty-seven minutes.
Below the fold, I try to explain what Curtis was talking about for those 27 minutes. It will take me quite a long post.
Background
NV1-based Diamond Edge
Swaaye
,
CC-By-SA 3.0
In the "Three Decades" section of
Engineering For The Long Term
I wrote:
The opportunity we saw when we started Nvidia was that the PC was transitioning from the PC/AT bus to version 1 of the PCI bus. The PC/AT bus' bandwidth was completely inadequate for 3D games, but the PCI bus had considerably more. Whether it was enough was an open question. We clearly needed to make the best possible use of the limited bandwidth we could get.
We had two basic ways of making "the best possible use of the limited bandwidth":
Reduce the amount of data we needed to ship across the bus for a given image.
Increase the amount of data shipped in each cycle of the bus.
Imaging Model
A triangle is the simplest possible description of a surface. Thus almost the entire history of 3D computer graphics has modeled the surfaces of 3D objects using triangles. But there is a technique, dating back at least to Robert Mahl's 1972 paper
Visible Surface Algorithms for Quadric Patches
, for modeling curved surfaces directly. It takes a lot more data to describe a quadric patch than a triangle. But to achieve equivalent realism you need so many fewer patches that the amount of data for each frame is reduced by a significant factor.
Virtua Fighter on NV1
As far as I know at the time only Sega in the video game industry used quadric patches. When we launched NV1 at Comdex we were able to show Sega arcade games such as
Virtua Fighter
running on a PC at full frame rate, a first for the industry. The reason was that NV1 used quadric patches and thus made better use of the limited PCI bus bandwidth.
At Sun, James Gosling and I built the extremely sophisticated and forward-looking but proprietary
NeWS window system
. At the same time, I also worked with engineers at competitors such as Digital Equipment to build the
X Window System
. One of my many learning experiences at Sun came early in the
long history of the X Window System
. It rapidly became obvious to me that there was no way NeWS could compete with the much simpler, open-source X. I argued for Sun to open-source NeWS and failed. I argued for Sun to drop NeWS and adopt X, since that was what application developers wanted. Sun wasted precious time being unable to decide what to do, finally deciding not to decide and wasting a lot of resource merging NeWS and X into a kludge that was a worse NeWS and a worse X than its predecessors. This was just one of a number of fights at Sun I lost (
this discusses another
).
Once Microsoft announced
Direct X
it was obvious to me that Nvidia was doomed if the next chip did quadric patches, because the developers would have to work with Direct X's triangles. But, like Sun, Nvidia seemed unable to decide to abandon its cherished technology. Time for a decision to be effective was slipping away. I quit, hoping to shake things up so as to enable a decision to do triangles. It must have worked. The books recount how close Nvidia was to bankruptcy when RIVA 128 shipped. The rest is history for which I was just an observer.
I/O Architecture
In contrast the I/O architecture was, over time, the huge success we planned. Kim
writes (Page 95)
:
Early on, Curtis Priem had invented a "virtualized objects" architecture that would be incorporated in all of Nvidia's chips. It became an even bigger advantage for the company once Nvidia adopted the faster cadence of chip releases. Priem's design had a software based "resource manager", essentially a miniature operating system that sat on top of the hardware itself. The resource manager allowed Nvidia's engineers to emulate certain hardware features that normally needed to be physically printed onto chip circuits. This involved a performance cost but

data.title: Show HN: Juvio – UV Kernel for Jupyter
data.author: okost1
data.article_summary: Juvio 是一个为 Jupyter Notebook 设计的 kernel，提供可重现、依赖感知和 Git 友好的功能。它支持在笔记本中直接管理依赖，通过 %juvio install 命令安装包，并将依赖作为元数据保存，确保环境一致性。Juvio 自动在临时虚拟环境中安装所需依赖，并使用 # %% 标记将笔记本转换为脚本格式，便于版本控制。使用步骤包括安装 Juvio 和 uv，启动 JupyterLab 并创建 Juvio 笔记本，然后安装所需包和运行代码。Juvio 无需额外锁定或需求文件，保证可重现性，并使 Git diff 更简洁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Juvio项目的实施及其应用场景

不同观点：
• [积极支持和期待尝试] heisenzombie表示对Juvio项目期待已久，并计划尝试。他认为该项目对他当前的用例非常有帮助，尤其是在管理大量"写一次，偶尔重跑"的笔记本方面。他目前通过语义版本控制和定期创建新内核来管理依赖关系，但认为这不是理想状态。
• [关注具体实现细节] flakiness对"git友好格式"表示赞赏，并询问markdown单元格的具体实现方式，是否作为Python注释嵌入。
• [简单支持] simlevesque简单表达了对项目的赞赏，并表示会尝试使用。
• [兼容性问题] antman关注Juvio是否能在Jupyter Lite上运行，提出了对项目适用范围的疑问。
• [质疑和不解] imcritic对Juvio的介绍中提到的"不需要额外的锁或需求文件"以及"保证可重复性"的具体含义表示不解，认为需要更清晰的解释来理解项目的实际用途。

补充讨论：
• [相关项目推荐] jwilber提到了另一个相关项目Juv，提供了GitHub链接以供参考。

争议焦点：
• Juvio项目的具体实现细节和应用场景尚不清晰，尤其是对于新用户或潜在用户（如imcritic）而言，需要更详细的解释来理解其优势和用途。
• 兼容性问题，特别是是否支持Jupyter Lite，是用户关注的一个重要方面。

Juvio
: reproducible, dependency-aware, and Git-friendly Jupyter Notebooks.
🚀 What It Does
💡
Inline Dependency Management
Install packages right from the notebook:
%
juvio
install
numpy
pandas
Dependencies are saved directly in the notebook as metadata (PEP 723-style), like:
# /// script
# requires-python = "==3.10.17"
# dependencies = [
# "numpy==2.2.5",
# "pandas==2.2.3"
# ]
# ///
⚙️
Automatic Environment Setup
When the notebook is opened, Juvio installs the dependencies automatically in an ephemeral virtual environment (using
uv
), ensuring that the notebook runs with the correct versions of the packages and Python.
📁
Git-Friendly Format
Notebooks are converted on the fly to a script-style format using
# %%
markers, making diffs and version control painless:
# %%
%
juvio
install
numpy
# %%
import
numpy
as
np
# %%
arr
=
np
.
array
([
1
,
2
,
3
])
print
(
arr
)
# %%
🧑‍💻 How to Use
1. Install Juvio:
pip install juvio
jupyter labextension
enable
juvio-frontend
2. Make sure you have uv installed:
https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/
3. Start JupyterLab and create a Juvio Notebook.
4. Install necessary packages in the notebook and run your code
%
juvio
install
...
Dependencies are tracked, environments are reproducible, and your notebook stays Git-clean ✨
Why Use Juvio?
No additional lock or requirements files are needed
Guaranteed reproducibility
Cleaner Git diffs

data.title: 27000 Dragons and 10'000 Lights: GPU-Driven Clustered Forward Renderer
data.author: logdahl
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种GPU驱动的集群前向渲染器，能够在GTX 1070显卡上以1080p分辨率、60fps以上的帧率渲染27,000个斯坦福龙模型和10,000个光源。传统渲染器中，CPU和GPU之间存在数据分离，CPU负责实体数据，GPU负责纹理和网格数据。这种设计通常需要为每个对象单独绘制，导致大量绘制调用。为了提高性能，作者使用GPU驱动的方法，通过间接多绘制（indirect multi draws）技术，将对象数据保存在连续的缓冲区中，并在帧渲染前将修改的数据上传到GPU。通过计算着色器进行可见性剔除，减少不必要的绘制调用，从而显著提升渲染效率。该方法优化了内存使用和绘制调用，实现了高性能的并行渲染。

logdahl.net / 27'000 dragons and 10'000 lights: GPU-Driven Clustered Forward Renderer
2025/04/15
During the course
Advanced Computer Graphics and Applications
I had lots of time (and freedom!) to develop something interesting. While this is an article about computer graphics, it's also about high-performance parallelization strategies.
I have written a GPU-Driven forward rendering using clustered shading. It can render 27'000 stanford dragons with 10'000 lights at 1080p in over 60fps on a GTX 1070 GPU. In this post, I will present exactly how my renderer achieves this performance.
dragons.
GPU-Driven What?
In a conventional renderer, there is a certain kind of separation in memory and ownership between the GPU and CPU. Usually, the GPU owns texture data, meshes and other assets—while the CPU owns entity data (position, velocity, etc). This is usually a good design, as the entity data is modified many times on the CPU and uploaded once (through a uniform or similar) for each frame to the GPU.
This however, means that certain barriers need to be put up between writing the per-object data and rendering it. Importantly, using a single uniform for all objects requires that each object is rendered sequentially in it's own draw call.
Our goal is to reduce the number of draw calls to as few as possible. In both GL and Vulkan, there is exists an API for
indirect multi draws
. These differ from normal draw calls in that the CPU dispatches the instruction with the draw details (index count, start vertex index) already present on the GPU in a buffer. This way, a single API call can execute multiple draw calls. It results in a few limitations —for example, re-binding resources or changing shaders between draw calls is not possible—but is a tradeoff for performance.
In my renderer, the entity (object) data is kept in a contigous buffer, and any modifications to it are marked. Before rendering a frame, all modified parts are uploaded to the GPU.

In the above figure, the GPU buffers chosen are shown. As some other renderers do, we share a single GPU buffer for all vertex data. Instead, we use a simple allocator which manages this contigous buffer automatically. This is done for the index buffer as well. There is a drawback to doing this; it requires all vertices to have the same format (same attributes). This can be a problem if there are many different types of meshes in a scene. One solution can be to have a separate vertex buffers for some attributes, which may also improve performance due to cache coherency. For example, one might want to make a separate buffer for animated vertices, or a separate buffer for only the animation attributes (bone ids, weights, etc.).
We also have some unique buffers to this system; namely, the
Object Buffer
and the
Draw Buffer
. These contains information that a conventional CPU-driven renderer must provide to the GPU every frame, but are instead stored on device. Objects that are fully static (terrain for example) only needs to be uploaded once. The draw buffer is what actually reduces the number of CPU draw calls (using the aforementioned
draw indirect
API).
Draw Call Generation
For an optimized renderer, we want to cull objects that are outside the main camera frustum. As you can see from the buffer diagram, we actually have everything we need (except for the camera) to determine what needs to be rendered. As we now create draw calls (into the
Draw Buffer
) from the GPU, the GPU is now able to cull the scene, which should come with significant speed improvements.
I simplified this by having the meshes store an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB). While other shapes could be used (just prepend a flag), this works well in my cases.

• [observationist] 对[rbrownmh]提到的项目中的技术细节进行了解释，特别是针对NACA 4位数代码与翼型形状的关系，提供了一个参考链接帮助理解。
• [ge96] 关注了[rbrownmh]项目中的一个有趣功能，即摄像机移动，并用幽默的方式表达了对该功能的惊讶和兴趣。
• [hbrav] 有流体动力学背景，表示愿意帮助[rbrownmh]的项目，并询问如何取得联系，显示出对实际技术应用的兴趣和合作意愿。

data.title: OpenAI Codex hands-on review
data.author: fragmede
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Codex的工作原理、优点以及待改进之处。Codex是一个通过聊天界面管理代码任务的工具，用户需订阅Pro版或获得邀请才能使用。它可以克隆用户的GitHub仓库并在沙盒中执行任务，适合管理多个项目。优点包括可以通过自然语言并行处理多个任务，支持快速切换项目，符合高效工作流程的需求，且未来有望实现远程工作。但目前Codex的错误处理不佳，代码质量和大型任务执行仍需改进，且无法在现有分支上流畅迭代更新。此外，沙盒缺乏网络连接，限制了某些开发任务的使用。整体而言，Codex在简化日常维护任务上表现出色，但复杂任务处理仍需优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的Codex工具的使用体验、功能和潜在影响

不同观点：
• [rmonvfer] 认为Codex的用户体验不佳，特别是在等待时间和环境定义方面存在问题。他还指出Codex与互联网隔离，限制了其自主研究能力。相比之下，他认为Claude在处理复杂应用时表现更好，支持快速找到错误。

• [teekert] 理想化地希望AI能帮助处理任务规划，从而有更多时间享受自然，但同时也指出这种理想可能导致职业转变。

Things I'm waiting on to improve
Poor error handling
Code quality and one-shot task execution
Multi-turn updates on a branch
Lack of network connectivity in execution sandboxes
Did it unlock insane productivity gains for me?
Codex: How it works
Codex is currently a chat-first experience. You gain access by being invited or by paying for the Pro ($200/per month) subscription.
Once you've got access, you start by enabling multi-factor authentication, which is required to use Codex. Next, you authorize the Codex GitHub app for each organization you want it to work with.
Codex then clones your repositories into its own sandboxes so it can run commands and create branches on your behalf.
If you maintain dozens of public and private repositories, this setup is fantastic because you can jump between projects and queue up tasks for each of them without leaving the interface.
If you only keep a single repo or two, the overhead may feel heavier than just asking an LLM for help or working in an AI-powered editor like Cursor.
Things I like about Codex
Consciousness and desire are multi-threaded
Codex feels like it was designed for me.
This GitHub connection allows you to specify which repository and which branch your current instructions are for, because the primary chat interface is contemplated as a place for you to
rapid-fire a day's worth of tasks into the interface to spin up multiple tasks in parallel.
I took a swing through the Codex best practices guide, which encourages you to spin up as many tasks as you need. The current rate limits support you doing this.
This is one of the things I like most about Codex and that I'm most excited for as the platform improves, because this gels with the way I work.
By the time I start work, I tend to have a laundry list of items I want to complete, so initiating a ton of them in parallel via natural language feels like a reasonable interface.
I think this will eventually support my dream untethered workflow
As I wrote about in
Walking and talking with AI in the woods
, ideally I'd like to start my morning in an office, launch a bunch of tasks,
get some planning out of the way, and then step out for a long walk in nature.
Codex is usable from my phone even today:
I think, ultimately, once some of the sharp edges are polished, Codex will support me and others in performing our work effectively away from our desks.
Follow ups via chat
Once your initial task has had some time to bake, you can click into it to view its progress, see the logs and make follow-up requests via a very familiar chat interface.
Looks good - ship it!
Once you're satisfied with the changes on a given branch, you can tell Codex to open a PR for you, and it will automatically
fill in the description.
Monitor logs and progress of tasks
You can step into any tasks to see the chat pane but also the raw logs, which show you the commands and shells that Codex is spawning
in order to make changes.
Things I'm waiting on to improve
Poor error handling
Starting tasks fails. Opening pull requests fails.
Why?
Who knows.
Code quality and one-shot task execution
I've been experimenting with Codex for about 3 days at the time of writing. I haven't yet noticed a marked difference in the performance of the Codex model, which OpenAI explains is a descendant of GPT-3 and is proficient in more
than 12 programming languages.
Right now, it feels like I can spin up multiple tasks in parallel with a 40-60% chance that I'll be content enough with the result to hit the Open PR button instead of requesting changes.
So far Codex has been perfect for firing off a bunch of maintenance-level updates: minor copy tweaks, style changes and other small chores. I've tried asking it to tackle larger refactors and the experience quickly becomes cumbersome. The current workflow wants to open a fresh pull request for every iteration, which means pushing follow-up commits to an existing branch is awkward at best.
Multi-turn updates on a branch
Updating existing PRs is rough.
It's not clear when or if changes will be pushed on an existing branch, and right now the app encourages you to create more pull requests.
That makes multi-step refactors tricky because you can't reliably iterate on the same branch within Codex. Until this becomes smoother, I plan to use it mainly for the quick wins that can ship in a single pass.
Lack of network connectivity in execution sandboxes
To be clear, I understand this is an intentional design choice. It mitigates remote code execution vulnerabilities amongst others.

data.title: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
data.author: akarshkumar0101
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出了“破碎纠缠表征假说”（Fractured Entangled Representation, FER），质疑仅通过提升性能是否意味着内部表征的优化。研究比较了通过开放搜索进化的网络与传统随机梯度下降（SGD）训练的网络在生成单一图像任务中的表现。尽管两者输出相似，但内部表征显著不同。SGD训练的网络表现出破碎纠缠的表征（FER），而进化网络更接近统一因子化表征（UFR）。大规模模型中，FER可能影响泛化、创造力等核心能力。因此，理解和缓解FER对表征学习至关重要。文章还提供了代码和数据可视化，帮助重现和进一步研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：神经网络中的表示形式及其解释性

不同观点：
• **scarmig**：关注除了随机梯度下降（SGD）以外的其他搜索过程，特别是那些被称为“生物学上合理”的算法（如forward-forward算法）。他提问这些算法中的内部表示是否更接近于“破碎的”或“统一的”表示形式。

• **cwmoore**：提出了一种简化的视角，将其类比为“mirroronic gravitation”，但没有深入展开讨论。

• **goldemerald**：认为文章缺少对线性表示假说（linear representation hypothesis）的引用，指出近期关于神经网络可解释性的研究显示单个神经元是多义的，因此对可解释性没有实际帮助。他建议通过线性探针或稀疏自动编码器来揭示语义属性，并提到Neel Nanda的实验以及其他相关研究。

• **ipunchghosts**：赞赏文章使用权重衰减（weight decay）来评估假设，认为这是引发结构化表示的重要方法。他进一步提出，权重衰减作为层深度的指数函数应用时，结果会有所改善。

• **timewizard**：对现代AI通过扩展现有系统来提升性能的做法表示怀疑，认为如果性能提升只是线性的，那就没有值得兴奋的地方，可能进入了一个死胡同。

• **light_hue_1**：对“破碎的表示”这一概念提出质疑，认为没有数学上的定义，仅仅是个人审美偏好。他强调个人偏好不能预测网络的有效性，并回顾了古典AI和图形模型的失败经验，呼吁停止这种做法以避免重蹈覆辙。

补充讨论：
• **akarshkumar0101**：提供了一个推特链接和一篇论文链接，可能为讨论提供了额外的背景资料或相关研究。

争议焦点：
• **表示形式的定义和评价标准**：不同研究者对“破碎的表示”和“统一的表示”有不同的理解和评价标准，light_hue_1更是直接质疑其数学定义和实用价值。
• **神经网络可解释性的实用性**：goldemerald和light_hue_1对神经元的多义性和可解释性的实际应用价值存在分歧。

整体来看，讨论围绕神经网络表示形式的性质、可解释性以及不同算法和方法在其中的作用展开，反映了学术界对这一复杂问题的多角度思考。

The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
📝
Paper PDF
Akarsh Kumar

Abstract
Much of the excitement in modern AI is driven by the observation that scaling up existing systems leads to better performance.
But does better performance necessarily imply better internal representations?
While the representational optimist assumes it must, this position paper challenges that view.
We compare neural networks evolved through an open-ended search process to networks trained via conventional stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on the simple task of generating a single image.
This minimal setup offers a unique advantage: each hidden neuron's full functional behavior can be easily visualized as an image, thus revealing how the network's output behavior is internally constructed neuron by neuron.
The result is striking: while both networks produce the same output behavior, their internal representations differ dramatically.
The SGD-trained networks exhibit a form of disorganization that we term
fractured entangled representation
(FER).
Interestingly, the evolved networks largely lack FER, even approaching a
unified factored representation
(UFR).
In large models, FER may be degrading core model capacities like generalization, creativity, and (continual) learning.
Therefore, understanding and mitigating FER could be critical to the future of representation learning.

Running Locally
To run this project locally, you can start by cloning this repo.
git clone https://github.com/akarshkumar0101/fer
Then, set up the python environment with conda:
conda create --name=fer python=3.10.16 --yes
conda activate fer
Now you can install these libraries.
The versioning needs to be very specific for the following.
However, if you don't need to train the SGD network to play around with the results; in that case you can simply install the cpu version of jax following

.

python -m pip install flax==0.10.2 evosax==0.1.6 orbax-checkpoint==0.11.0 optax==0.2.4 --no-deps
Then, install all the other necessary python libraries:
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

src/fer.ipynb
that quickly covers everything you need.

data.title: Production tests: a guidebook for better systems and more sleep
data.author: mcapodici
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了生产环境测试（production tests）在确保网站高可用性方面的重要性。现代软件工程通过自动化测试和可观察性工具保证质量，但生产环境测试能提供即时的故障通知，帮助在客户发现问题前进行修复。文章介绍了生产环境测试的基本概念，例如使用无头浏览器或API模拟用户行为，建议测试应在30秒内完成，并与报警系统或日志集成。生产环境测试有助于提高系统可靠性、辅助部署和问题诊断，还能缩短事故恢复时间。文章强调测试应简单可靠，避免复杂和误报，并给出了简单有效的测试示例，如登录验证、API调用等。复杂的测试可能导致资源消耗问题，因此需要谨慎设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生产环境测试（testing in production）的利弊与实施方案

不同观点：
• [hugs] 支持生产环境测试，提出建立去中心化的测试网络（如 'valet network'），认为可以利用真实设备和条件进行测试，但需要谨慎处理测试数据和系统日志。同时，个人对该方案的市场需求仍在探索中。
• [burnt-resistor] 将生产环境测试视为深度监控的一部分，主要用于检查功能可用性和正确性。
• [vasusen] 支持生产环境测试，并分享了WePay的经验，强调少量关键测试的重要性，帮助调试和警报。目前在Donobu构建自动化测试方案，将生产环境测试作为端到端测试的子类别。
• [ashishb] 提出"沿最小变化轴编写测试"的规则，认为这种测试更有价值且维护成本低。
• [testthetest] 对生产环境测试持谨慎态度，指出频繁测试会增加日志、指标和痕迹，且自动化测试可能被反垃圾系统过滤。建议使用"测试专用"用户代理或令牌来区分合成请求，但要注意这种做法可能导致"Volkswagen效应"。

补充讨论：
• [compumike] 提出生产环境测试的两种战术实施方式：(1) 外部服务发送HTTP响应或运行无头浏览器会话；(2) 内部定时任务进行断言检查并发送心跳信号。认为方式(2)更适合复杂应用，但也建议结合使用方式(1)进行全面监控，并分享了Heii On-Call工具的应用经验。此外，强调生产环境监控与CI测试的结合使用。

争议焦点：
• 生产环境测试的实际需求和实施复杂性。
• 测试频率与系统反垃圾机制之间的冲突。
• 使用"测试专用"用户代理或令牌的有效性和潜在副作用（Volkswagen效应）。

44013071.article_content:
Your customers expect your site to be fully working whenever they need it. This means you need to aim for near-perfect uptime not just for the site itself, but for all features customers may use.
Modern software engineering uses quality control measures such as automated test suites and observability tools (tracing, metrics, and logs) to ensure availability. Often overlooked in this landscape is
production tests
(also known as
synthetics
) that can give you immediate notification of failures in production.
Production tests can be setup up with minimal fuss—usually within one sprint—and can provide a high return on investment. In this post, I will cover how to best set up production tests and how they can help with reliability, deployments, and observability.
While I have always liked production tests, I got a real appreciation for them at Atlassian, where they are used extensively and are called “
pollinators
”, and I have seen first hand how they can give early warnings of problems, which can be fixed before the become incidents.
What are production tests?
A production test is any automated test that runs on the production environment. The test runs on a frequent schedule so that an on-call engineer can respond quickly. Typically, they run every minute. The test might use a headless browser to emulate user actions, or it may use an API directly to emulate the actions of browser code or backend service.
The production test should run in a reasonable time. I suggest 30 seconds or less, so that you can run the test easily once per minute. A test that takes longer than 30 seconds is probably to complex anyway for a production test. How the test deals with failure is up to your team. It could integrate with your on call paging system, send a Slack notification, or just log an error into your logging systems.
How do production tests help?
Productions tests help make your production environment more reliable by giving immediate warning of a regression. This means you can potentially fix issues before a customer discovers them.
In addition, the production test can be used as a canary before deployments, and as such acts as an integration test. The test can detect regressions that are caused by mismatches with other services, such as API shape or error-handling issues. You can run the test when deploying to development and staging environments too, to get a warning of an issue during development.
You also make it easier to debug production issues by having production tests. If you have an issue you are investigating, knowing which production tests are working and are failing gives you insight into what the issue might be. If you rely on other team’s services, and they also have production tests, you can look at their tests too to help with diagnostics.
Having production tests will reduce the time to recovery for any incident where a human has to fix it, as the engineer learns about the issue sooner, and has more information at hand to resolve it.
Important design considerations for production tests
For production-tests to be worth having, they need to be well-thought-out. If the test keeps failing it’ll probably get silenced and ignored. Even if the test is reliable it can cause other problems, such as resource usage impacting downstream systems. You may even have to change your systems to be a bit more testable. Here are some tips to consider when setting up your production tests:
Keep your production tests basic
Your production tests should cover less ground than your automated test suites. You want the tests to be reliable enough that they don’t waste your time with false alerts, which leads to frustration, lost time and possibly disabling of alerts. The goal of a production test is to be the canary that something has gone badly wrong. It gives you a head start on fixing it, hopefully before a customer gets affected.
To illustrate the required simplicity, here are some examples of what I think are good candidates for a production test:
Log in, and confirm you are on the home page, showing that user’s name.
Load the main editor of your app and type in Hello. Confirm Hello is there. Reload the browser and confirm Hello is still there.
Call 4 API endpoints to do CRUD operations for your microservice, using possibly some fake data in the API.
Ping /health and check for 200 response code within 250ms
Contrast this with these more complex and problematic production tests:
Run through a 25-step test that checks all the main functionality of the editor, asserting that elements are the correct size and are in the correct position.
Test that if you make call in quick succession to the API, they will be added to the database in the same order.
Check that the credit card page can differentiate between Visa and Mastercard based on the card number.
Ping /health and check for 200 response code within 1.5ms
The first examples are good because they are quick, reliable, and simple. They are not too functionality-specific, are so

data.title: The Last Letter
data.author: HR01
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者在法国波尔多一家书店避雨时，偶然发现一本收录了二战期间被纳粹行刑队处决者绝笔信的书。这些信件充满了临终者面对死亡的迫切与不可避免的情感，与日常书信、日记或政治论文不同，它们展现了人类在最后时刻的脆弱与真实。信中内容既个人又普遍，例如一位抵抗组织领袖罗伯特·贝克在信中对孩子温柔地解释他将 embark on a "big journey"，而另一位抵抗者雅克·博德里则直接告诉母亲他即将被夺去生命。这些信件揭示了人类在生死边缘时的深刻情感和哲学思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕二战时期死刑犯的遗书及其解读的讨论，涉及遗书的保存、内容真实性、哲学反思以及文章叙述方式。

不同观点：
• [bee_rider] 认为 Tony Bloncourt 的照片保存完好且风格现代，带来了认知上的不协调感，因为很难想象这样一个现代形象的人会被纳粹杀害。同时，对纳粹允许囚犯写遗书这一行为表示好奇，并探讨了遗书中关于生命与死亡的哲理性表达，特别是时态运用带来的反思。
• [bmink] 对文章的叙述方式提出批评，认为文章过长且过多关注主题的背景和作者自身的反思，而没有直接呈现遗书本身，导致读者无法直接读到信件内容。
• [yapyap] 对从遗书中学习人生哲理的观点持怀疑态度，认为这些遗书在纳粹审查下必然有所保留，不可能包含对纳粹的直接批评。此外，提出临终者的不可靠性，认为临终者的建议或反思可能受到自身偏见的影响，且因为对死者的尊重，人们往往不愿对这些遗书内容进行客观分析。

补充讨论：
• [bee_rider] 对遗书中“我将活过今天”这一表达的哲学性表现出浓厚兴趣，认为其通过时态选择巧妙地反映了生与死的间隔。
• [yapyap] 引用了一篇关于死亡临终谬误的文章，强调不应全盘接受临终者的建议或反思，因为这些可能受到临终时特殊心理状态的影响，且遗书内容可能因外部审查而失真。
• 争议的焦点在于遗书的真实性和解读的价值。一方面，遗书被视为承载深刻生命反思的文本；另一方面，遗书的撰写受到外部压力和临终心理状态的影响，可能并不完全真实或客观。

总体来看，讨论围绕遗书的真实性、哲学性及其在历史和人文背景下的解读展开，反映了不同读者对遗书内容及其呈现方式的多元看法。

On a wintry day in Bordeaux, France, I took refuge from the rain inside a cosy bookshop stacked to the ceiling with books. Place Gambetta, Bordeaux’s iconic square framed with majestic
18th-century
limestone façades, was under construction. ‘It’s always like this,’ the owner told me with a disparaging glare. I was not sure if the comment was directed at the rain or the construction. Inside, I browsed the shelves, soaking in the titles one by one. A book cast among thousands caught my eye:
La vie à en mourir: lettres de fusillés
(2003). It contained farewell letters of those shot by Nazi firing squads during the German occupation of France in the Second
World War.
I picked it up, opening the pages slowly and carefully as if I held in my hands a fragile treasure, like ‘this butterfly wing’ which the
19-year
-old Robert Busillet, executed for his role in an intelligence-gathering and sabotage network, bequeathed to his mother ‘
en souvenir de moi
’, to remember him by. I flitted through the pages, reading flashes of a letter here, longer passages there. As someone who studies war, I am no stranger to the theme of killing and dying. But this experience was different.
Last letters are unlike any other type of writing I have ever encountered. They are of a singular ilk because they peer into the souls of those confronting imminent and inescapable death. Different from everyday letters, diaries, memoirs, political tracts or philosophical treatises, because of the urgency that shapes the act of writing. The authors know there will not be another chance to say what must be said.
Each last letter is uniquely personal, yet there is a universal feel to them, almost as if they paint a naked portrait of the human condition. To read them incarnates the phrase penned by Michel de Montaigne. ‘If I were a maker of books,’ he wrote in the
16th century
, ‘I would make a register, with comments, of various deaths. He who would teach men to die would teach them to live.’
D
awn breaks on your final morn. A prison guard hands you a blank sheet of paper and a pen two hours before your execution by Nazi firing squad. The customs and traditions of the time – sometimes, but not always, respected by the Nazi authorities – permit the condemned a final act of communication: the last letter. To whom do you write? What do you say, knowing this is the last chance to
say it?
It’s not just the heroic resistors whom the Nazis executed. One could be killed for far less. In the autumn of 1941, the
Militärbefehlshaber in Frankreich
– the military commander who controlled Paris – enacted the ‘hostage code’, whereby all those in a state of incarceration are considered to be political hostages. In the event of a ‘terrorist attack’ – an act of armed resistance against the occupier – these political hostages could be executed in reprisal. In other words, those arrested and imprisoned for, let’s say, writing or distributing illegal tracts and newspapers, protesting in the streets, or even listening to news from forbidden radio sources such as the BBC were, effectively, handed death sentences-in-waiting.
I’ve read hundreds of last letters, written by armed resistors and political hostages alike. One day, I sat down to catalogue the ways in which the soon-to-be executed communicated to their loved ones the macabre news. It was an uncomfortable, but deeply moving, task.
‘Be courageous,
ma chérie
. It is no doubt the last time that I write you. Today, I will have lived’
‘I can give no longer any further testimony of my affection than this letter,’ began Robert Beck, the head of an active terrorist organisation, according to the Gestapo. ‘Colvert will never again see his Plouf, nor his little Plumette. He is leaving for a big big journey,’ he added, softening the blow for his children.
Jacques Baudry, who had resisted the Nazis since his high-school days when he organised protests and marches, later participating in armed attacks against the occupiers, was rather blunter in his letter to his mother: ‘They are going to rip me from this life that you gave me and that I clung
to so.’
Huynh Khuong An, a young high-school teacher arrested for possessing anti-fascist propaganda and related clandestine activities, was plucked from the cistern of political hostages one sunny October day. Writing to his lover, he implores: ‘Be courageous,
ma chérie
. It is no doubt the last time that I write you. Today, I will have lived.’
This turn of phrase, so simple grammatically speaking, is deceptively philosophical because it captures the interval that separates the writer from the reader, the one who will
have lived
from the one who
lives on
. Death was no longer on the horizon. The moment was decided, imminent and irrevocable.
To read the letters is to take a journey inward, deep into the world of emotions at the very frontier of living and dying. In one’s final moments, superficiality cuts away, revealing something meaningful and deep about the human condition. From Montai

• [bee_rider] 认为 Tony Bloncourt 的照片保存完好且风格现代，带来了认知上的不协调感，因为很难想象这样一个现代形象的人会被纳粹杀害。同时，对纳粹允许囚犯写遗书这一行为表示好奇，并探讨了遗书中关于生命与死亡的哲理性表达，特别是时态运用带来的反思。
• [bmink] 对文章的叙述方式提出批评，认为文章过长且过多关注主题的背景和作者自身的反思，而没有直接呈现遗书本身，导致读者无法直接读到信件内容。
• [yapyap] 对从遗书中学习人生哲理的观点持怀疑态度，认为这些遗书在纳粹审查下必然有所保留，不可能包含对纳粹的直接批评。此外，提出临终者的不可靠性，认为临终者的建议或反思可能受到自身偏见的影响，且因为对死者的尊重，人们往往不愿对这些遗书内容进行客观分析。

补充讨论：
• [bee_rider] 对遗书中“我将活过今天”这一表达的哲学性表现出浓厚兴趣，认为其通过时态选择巧妙地反映了生与死的间隔。
• [yapyap] 引用了一篇关于死亡临终谬误的文章，强调不应全盘接受临终者的建议或反思，因为这些可能受到临终时特殊心理状态的影响，且遗书内容可能因外部审查而失真。
• 争议的焦点在于遗书的真实性和解读的价值。一方面，遗书被视为承载深刻生命反思的文本；另一方面，遗书的撰写受到外部压力和临终心理状态的影响，可能并不完全真实或客观。

总体来看，讨论围绕遗书的真实性、哲学性及其在历史和人文背景下的解读展开，反映了不同读者对遗书内容及其呈现方式的多元看法。

data.title: Effort and Challenges in Building Embedded Audio DSP Software Across Platforms
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary:
嵌入式音频DSP开发耗时且复杂，尤其是在需要为高质量音频调优固件并将其应用于多个硬件平台或不同外形时。主要挑战包括：

1. **迭代周期成本高且周转慢**：每次调整音频参数需修改代码、重建固件并重新刷入设备，导致实验缓慢，难以进行即时的A/B对比。
   
2. **跨多硬件平台复用的复杂性**：音频DSP代码常针对特定处理器架构优化，移植到新平台需重写或重新优化，增加开发时间和风险。

3. **缺乏实时可配置性和可见性**：嵌入式系统缺乏实时调整参数和查看内部行为的工具，调试和调优过程如同“黑箱”，增加了难度和不确定性。

实时调优能力可大幅简化开发过程，避免重复的代码修改和重建，提高效率和音质。

44026413.article_content:
Embedded audio DSP development is notoriously time-consuming and complex, especially when firmware needs to be tuned for high-quality audio and reused on multiple hardware platforms or in different form-factors. Those inefficiencies are primarily the result of only a handful of challenges, which are, as yet, poorly addressed by existing tooling.
Iteration Cycles: High Cost and Slow Turnaround
Developing and tuning audio DSP firmware often requires many iterative cycles of coding, compiling, and testing. Each adjustment to an audio parameter typically means modifying code, rebuilding the firmware, and re-flashing the device, which is time-intensive and hampers quick experimentation. As a result, audio engineers cannot easily perform instantaneous A/B comparisons of different tunings.
One industry whitepaper
notes that "often, DSP engineers must rebuild and compile code for different sound settings", so by the time an engineer listens to a second or third tuning iteration, they've lost the fresh reference of how the first one sounded. This slow turnaround makes it costly to refine algorithms to optimal sound quality.
What makes iteration especially high-cost in audio is the subtlety of human hearing; tiny differences in filter coefficients or EQ settings can be discernible, meaning many fine-tuning passes are needed. Without real-time adjustments, each fine-tune is a full software cycle. In
How to Shorten and Simplify Embedded Audio Product Creation
, Dr. Beckman emphasizes that real-time tuning capability would greatly streamline this process, since it would eliminate the need to "change code and re-compile before it can be heard again," allowing the audio engineer to tweak parameters live and immediately hear the result. In current workflows, this capability is often lacking, stretching development over long debug/tune cycles.
Complexity of Reuse Across Multiple Hardware Platforms
The effort required to build an audio DSP stack multiplies when that software must run on different chipsets or DSP cores. Porting and generalizing DSP code across hardware is a major challenge: audio algorithms are frequently optimized for a specific processor architecture (sometimes even in hand-written assembly for performance), and these optimizations don't directly transfer to a new platform. A modular design is not common in traditional audio DSP firmware. Historically, "an audio post-processing algorithm was developed considering a specific DSP architecture", meaning the code was heavily tied to one chip's features and instruction set. When a new product uses a different DSP or a new SoC version, engineers often must re-write or re-optimize large portions of the code, effectively rebuilding the audio stack for each platform.
Moreover, audio DSP libraries have often been delivered as monolithic blocks combining many signal processing features. This monolithic approach hurts reusability. As one engineer noted, if a customer or new product only needs a subset of the features, the entire library might need to go through a full development cycle again to be adapted and retested for that subset. In other words, lack of modularity means code reuse across products is limited, leading to duplicated effort. Maintaining separate codebases for different chips also increases engineering overhead and risk of bugs. All of this adds complexity and time: teams must debug and tune on each platform's unique toolchain and hardware quirks.
Lack of Real-Time Configurability and Visibility
A common pain point in embedded DSP development is the lack of real-time configurability and internal visibility during development. Unlike software on a PC where developers can often tweak parameters on the fly, embedded audio firmware typically runs without a rich UI or console. Gaining insight into the DSP's behavior usually involves using hardware debuggers or adding instrumentation code. However, embedded systems have tight real-time constraints: even printing debug values can disturb timing. In fact, adding just a few
printf
statements can significantly affect performance (cache usage, timing, etc.), to the point that such instrumentation is often not usable for real-time audio code. Thus, developers operate with limited visibility into what the audio algorithms are doing in real time, making debugging and tuning akin to a "black box" process.
Not having real-time control is equally problematic for tuning audio performance. There is typically no live GUI to adjust filter coefficients or mixer levels on an embedded DSP in real time, so audio engineers must rely on slow compile-flash-listen cycles as described earlier. Beckman emphasizes that
real-time tuning
is highly desirable so that engineers could tweak multiple parameters live without full rebuilds. The lack of such interactive control not only slows down finding the best sound but also reduces confidence; if a change degrades audio, one might not catch it until much later. data.title: Hypervisor as a Library
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种在Starina操作系统中运行Linux应用程序的方法，通过在一个轻量级虚拟机中运行真实的Linux内核来实现Linux兼容性。文章首先提到一个简单的Go程序"catsay"，并引出在Starina上运行Linux程序的挑战。作者提出了一种设计模式，即将 hypervisor 作为库集成到操作系统中，而不是作为独立进程。

为了实现Linux兼容性，Starina采用运行真实Linux内核的方式，而非逐一模拟系统调用。文中展示了如何使用类似Rust中的`std::process::Command`模式在Starina中运行"catsay"程序，并详细解释了底层的hypervisor工作原理。通过创建虚拟机、安装Linux内核、处理内存映射I/O（MMIO）等步骤，Starina实现了与Linux的无缝集成。

文章最后强调，将hypervisor作为库使用可以提高灵活性和性能，而不必依赖进程隔离。这种方法尽管在云计算环境中可能面临硬件辅助虚拟化的问题，但对于Starina系统来说具有吸引力。

• apitman 的评论指出，文档或介绍中的表述可能不够清晰，尤其是在 hypervisor 是否原生实现的问题上，容易让人产生误解。
• Onavo 通过提到 Microsoft Hyperlight，可能在暗示 Starina 使用 QEMU 作为后端是一种常见的技术选择，或者在引导讨论往其他类似技术方案上发展。

争议焦点：Starina 是否原生实现了 hypervisor 功能，还是依赖 QEMU 作为后端实现。这涉及到技术实现的细节和用户对 Starina 架构理解的准确性。

44038279.article_content:
Before we dive into the topic, let me introduce you my new friend
catsay
, a simple Go program which eats stdin and speaks like a cat:
Cute! ... but it's not what I want to talk about. What makes this screenshot very exciting is, it's a Linux lightweight virtual machine running on
Starina operating system
!
That said, this post is not about how hard it is to write a hypervisor (see
my previous post
for that). In fact, it's not that hard. The hardest part is to design how you interact with the hypervisor. In other words, designing the hypervisor API. Starina needs an attractive integration with Linux.
In this post, I'd share a design pattern:
hypervisor as a library
.
How do we run Linux apps in Linux today?
First, if you were to write a Rust application which uses
catsay
, how do you integrate?
In Rust, you would use
std::process::Command
to run
catsay
:
Command
::
new
(
"/bin/catsay"
)
.
stdin
(stdin)
.
spawn
()
If you want to pass an environment variable, just add a single line:
Command
::
new
(
"/bin/catsay"
)
.
stdin
(stdin)
.
env
(
"CATSAY_MODE"
,
"dog"
)
.
spawn
()
Nice. If you're interested in its output, add another parameter
.stdout
:
let
child
=
Command
::
new
(
"/bin/catsay"
)
.
stdin
(stdin)
.
env
(
"CATSAY_MODE"
,
"dog"
)
.
stdout
(
Stdio
::
piped
())
.
spawn
()
It's boringly obvious, right? However, on another OS like Starina, it's not obvious how to provide a Linux environment, or Linux compatibility.
Linux compatibility
Providing Linux compatibility is a challenging task, and there are some ways to achieve it. A popular way is to run Linux binaries as kinda
in native
: hook system calls and emulate them. Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL 1) and FreeBSD Linuxulator are examples.
In Starina, I took a different approach:
run the real Linux kernel in a lightweight virtual machine
.
It might sound extreme, but it's already proven to be practical by WSL2. It has a huge drawback in the cloud computing environment where hardware-assisted virtualization is not available (or is slow) in cheap VM-based instances, but it's still attractive for Starina:
The interface between Linux and Starina is clearer: Virtio virtual devices.
Unlike FreeBSD, Starina is not that similar to Linux. Especially, I don't have a good idea to implement
fork(2)
efficiently without adding a tailor-made logic to the microkernel.
It is the genuine Linux kernel. No need to implement Linux system calls one by one, nor to discover every lesser-known features like
auxiliary vector
.
std::process::Command
for Linux VM
So, running the real Linux kernel in a lightweight VM sounds technically possible. However, how do we actually use it? My answer is, follow the
std::process::Command
pattern!
Here's how you can run
catsay
in Starina:
use
core
::
str
::
from_utf8;
use
starina
::
prelude
::*
;
use
starina_linux
::
BufferedStdin
;
use
starina_linux
::
BufferedStdout
;
pub
fn
catsay
(text
:
&
str
) {
let
stdin
=
BufferedStdin
::
new
(text);
let
stdout
=
BufferedStdout
::
new
();
starina_linux
::
Command
::
new
(
"/bin/catsay"
)
.
stdin
(stdin)
.
stdout
(stdout
.
clone
())
.
spawn
()
.
expect
(
"failed to execute process"
);
info!
(
"{}"
,
from_utf8
(
&
stdout
.
buffer
())
.
unwrap
());
}
Doesn't it look familiar?
How the hypervisor works
Under the hood,
starina_linux::Command
creates a lightweight VM using Starina's
HvSpace
(guest-physical address space) and
vCPU
(virtual CPU) APIs.
Here's a simplified version of
starina_linux::Command
:
let
mut
virtio_fs
=
VirtioFs
::
new
();
virtio_fs
.
add_file
(
"/stdin"
, stdin);
virtio_fs
.
add_file
(
"/stdout"
, stdout);
let
ram
=
Folio
::
allocate
(
MEMORY_SIZE
);
// folio = a memory region
install_device_tree
(
&mut
ram);
extract_linux_image
(
&mut
ram,
include_bytes!
(
"linux.bin"
));
let
hvspace
=
HvSpace
::
new
();
let
vcpu
=
Vcpu
::
new
(
&
hvspace);
loop
{
let
exit
=
vcpu
.
run
();
match
exit {
Reboot
=>
{
break
;
}
PageFault
{ gpaddr, data }
if
gpaddr
.
is_in_mmio
()
=>
{
virtio_fs
.
handle_mmio_access
(gpaddr, data);
}
_
=>
{
panic!
(
"unexpected VM exit reason: {:?}"
, exit);
}
}
}
In a nutshell, create a guest-physical address space, install Linux kernel into it, enter the VM world, and handle MMIO accesses.
Isn't it surprisingly simple? Linux KVM API also works in the similar way. Hypervisor is generally a very simple program (otherwise we would not trust it as a security boundary).
You might notice a mysterious
virtio_fs
object. As its name suggests, it's a virtual file system to provide a seamless integration with Starina. In Linux, stdin you provide is accessible as
/virtfs/stdin
and our custom init connects it to
catsay
.
Hypervisor as a library
A hypervisor, more specifically virtual machine monitor (VMM) such as QEMU and Firecracker, is typically used as a separate process. Your control plane program talks to them over an IPC mechanism. Having a process isolation is a good thing for security, but it limits the flexibility of integration and performance.

不同观点：
• [AdmiralAsshat] 认为Kobo接受了Google的支付系统，可以在Android应用内直接购买，虽然Google从中抽成，但改善了用户的购买体验，尤其是小额冲动消费。然而，Kobo礼品卡不能用于手机端购买。
• [thepryz] 提出，从技术上讲，通过Google、Amazon等平台获得的数字书籍实际上只是购买了许可，而非真正拥有，这一区别虽然细微但重要。
• [oldpersonintx2] 指出Anna's Archive的收费标准没有变化，暗示平台的收费政策并不统一。
• [SoftTalker] 认为大平台之间可能存在合谋和欺诈行为，且无人能够制止。
• [palata] 对Google和Amazon的声明表示怀疑，质疑为何只有少数公司能享受非Google支付选项，认为这可能涉及不公平待遇。
• [iLoveOncall] 反驳有关Amazon通过特殊协议避免支付Google费用的说法，认为Amazon可能通过与出版商的协议来保持盈利，且手机端购买用户的占比可能较低，因此Amazon愿意承受这部分损失以维持用户体验。

• 争议的焦点之一是Amazon是否通过特殊协议避免了Google的支付费用，以及这种协议是否存在不公平竞争。
• 另一个讨论点是数字书籍购买的性质，强调用户只是获得使用权而非所有权。
• 还有对大平台间潜在合谋行为的质疑，以及对平台政策透明度的关注。
• 最后，媒体在报道平台相关新闻时的公正性也被提及。

data.title: Autopsy of an LHC Beam Dump
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: CERN首次对大型强子对撞机（LHC）的放射性束流吸收器进行了“解剖”分析，以研究材料在高能束流冲击下的行为。由于运行十年后出现降解迹象，LHC的两个外部束流吸收器在停机期间被更换。为了解决氮气泄漏问题并为即将到来的Run 3及高光度LHC（HL-LHC）设计新吸收器，团队进行了详细检查。结果显示，挤压石墨盘出现裂纹，但低密度和高密度石墨块状况良好。此次分析确认了Run 3中继续使用低密度和高密度石墨，但排除了挤压石墨的使用。进一步研究正在HiRadMat设施进行，以测试HL-LHC的新材料。现有吸收器经过改良后应能承受Run 3增加的能量冲击。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• barbazoo引用了ChatGPT对大型强子对撞机（LHC）中束流倾卸系统的解释，关注CERN设施中的安全和操作系统的技术细节，强调其功能性和安全性。

补充讨论：
• RetroTechie的观点集中在视觉和审美层面，将尖端科技与娱乐文化（如游戏）联系起来，体现了科技在公众视野中的形象。
• barbazoo的评论则转向技术细节，提供关于束流倾卸系统的具体信息，突出了CERN在实际操作中的安全考虑和工程复杂性。

Autopsy of an LHC beam dump
For the first time at CERN, an autopsy has been carried out on a radioactive beam dump. Inspection of the inner workings of the device helped the teams to find out more about how materials behave under the impact of high-energy beams
8 June, 2022
|
By
Anaïs Schaeffer
The beam dump is moved into the radiation airlock installation specially constructed for the autopsy.
(Image: CERN)
During LS2, the LHC’s two external beam dumps were removed from the tunnel and replaced with spare ones. After ten years of operation, they were showing signs of degradation, notably nitrogen leaks. Before being installed, the spare dumps were modified and upgraded to prevent the same problems from occurring during Run 3 (see
this
Bulletin
article
published in 2020).
To find out more about the cause of the nitrogen leaks, an endoscopy was carried out in July 2020. It revealed unexpected cracks in the beam dump’s two extruded graphite discs (see box). An action plan was drawn up by the SY-STI (Sources, Targets and Interactions) group as more information was needed with Run 3 on the horizon, especially with a view to designing new spare beam dumps for the LHC and, beyond that, beam dumps for the HL-LHC. To access the dump’s three main components – high-density, low-density and extruded graphite (see below) – there was only one possible solution: perform an “autopsy” on one of the dumps. Given its radioactivity levels, this was easier said than done.
“To reach the heart of the beam dump, we needed to be able to open it…,” says project leader Ana-Paula Bernardes. “But its duplex-stainless-steel-alloy housing was extremely difficult to cut. The first attempt, in January 2021, under a framework contract, was unsuccessful: it was impossible to cut through it manually without exceeding the radiation dose limits. We considered outsourcing the job to a specialised external company with the right equipment for the task, but the costs and time frames were incompatible with the project.”
Top: Longitudinal test cut with the circular saw, performed by the SY-STI group. Solution chosen for the cutting of the radioactive dump. Middle: Positioning of the automated, rail-mounted circular saw for the first radial cut, performed by the SY-STI group. Bottom: The first longitudinal cut.
(Images: CERN)
Thanks to the expertise and versatility of CERN’s teams, a solution was eventually found in house: the SY-STI and BE-CEM (Controls, Electronics and Mechatronics) groups worked together to develop two techniques that would allow the dump’s housing to be cut remotely. The first involved an automated circular saw mounted on a rail, and the second a robot arm equipped with a cutter.
Longitudinal test cut with the robot arm, performed by the BE-CEM group. (Image: CERN)
Several trial runs were carried out on a mock-up in order to “choreograph” the operation and thus limit, as far as possible, the time spent in close proximity to the dump. The circular saw was ultimately used to make five cuts, in a radiation airlock installation created specially for the job: two radial cuts to separate the low-density graphite block and three longitudinal cuts to remove the stainless-steel-alloy housing.
The highly radioactive stainless-steel-alloy housing is removed by the EN-HE (Handling Engineering) group to allow access to the low-density graphite.(Image: CERN)
“As the endoscopy had already shown, both extruded graphite discs were cracked. Against all expectations, the low-density graphite was generally in good condition, as were the high-density-graphite blocks,” says Ana-Paula Bernardes.
The upstream extruded graphite disc (the first to be hit by the beam) is cracked. (Image: CERN)
“It was important to check the condition of the various components of the dump and establish how resistant they were, for various reasons,” explains Marco Calviani, leader of the Targets, Collimators and Dumps (STI-TCD) section in the SY department. “First of all, we needed to be sure that the dumps currently installed in the LHC – which are built from the same components as the autopsied dump – would withstand the energy levels of Run 3; next, we wanted to know what strategy to adopt for the two new spare dumps, which we need to design and manufacture by 2023, and especially for the dumps for the future HL-LHC.”
The results of the autopsy validated the use of low-density and high-density graphite for Run 3, but ruled out the use of extruded graphite for the design of the spare dumps. Other studies are under way at the HiRadMat facility (see the corresponding article entitled
“What will the future LHC beam dumps be made of?”
) to confirm these results and to test new materials, notably for the HL-LHC beam dumps. data.title: Gemini 2.5: Our most intelligent models are getting even better
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 谷歌发布Gemini 2.5系列更新，其中包括多项改进和新增功能。Gemini 2.5 Pro在编码和学术基准测试中表现优异，现已成为WebDev Arena和LMArena排行榜的领先模型，并在学习辅助方面获得广泛认可。新功能包括Deep Think模式，这是一种增强推理能力的新实验模式，已在复杂数学和编码测试中取得高分。此外，2.5 Pro和2.5 Flash模型增加了原生音频输出、高级安全保障和Project Mariner的计算机使用功能。2.5 Flash模型经过优化，效率更高，现已向开发者和企业开放预览，并将于六月全面推出。这些更新旨在提升开发者体验和模型性能，同时确保技术发布的安全性和责任性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新发布的2.5 Pro模型的表现及LLM（大型语言模型）版本更新和改进的相关争议

不同观点：
• **cye131** 认为新发布的2.5 Pro模型并没有达到宣称的100万上下文窗口的有效使用能力，尤其是在处理超过5万 tokens 时，生成逻辑块的能力不足。他还指出，新模型似乎在创造力和开放性任务上的表现不如从前，更注重于封闭式编程任务的表现，这可能是当前LLM发展的普遍趋势。

• **mchusma** 表达了对频繁版本更新的不满，认为新版本并不总是各方面都更好，反而增加了复杂性。他建议如果不能全面改进，不如直接发布2.6版本。

• **Aeolun** 表示自己经常看到其他模型的评分提高，但在实际使用时体验不佳，因此更倾向于使用Claude模型。他认为Claude模型的优势在于不会在未有实际改进时进行更新。

• **russfink** 提出一个技术性建议，询问公司为何不发布AI生成答案的哈希值，以便像教师这样的用户能够验证AI是否生成了特定的结果。

补充讨论：
• **关于模型表现的争议**：cye131和Aeolun都对新模型的实际表现提出了质疑，前者基于技术细节和任务表现，后者基于个人使用体验。

• **关于版本更新的争议**：mchusma对版本频繁更新持批评态度，认为这增加了不必要的复杂性，而Aeolun则赞赏Claude模型在更新上的谨慎态度。

• **关于验证机制的讨论**：russfink提出的哈希值建议引发了对AI生成结果验证机制的讨论，这是一个技术性和实用性兼具的问题。

Gemini 2.5: Our most intelligent models are getting even better
May 20, 2025
·

Share
Twitter

Gemini 2.5 Pro continues to be loved by developers as the best model for coding, and 2.5 Flash is getting even better with a new update. We’re also bringing new capabilities to our models, including Deep Think, an experimental enhanced reasoning mode for 2.5 Pro.
Tulsee Doshi
Senior Director, Product Management, on behalf of the Gemini team
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
In March, we announced
Gemini 2.5 Pro
, our most intelligent model yet, and two weeks ago, we brought you our
I/O update early
for developers to build incredible web apps. Today, we’re sharing even more updates to our
Gemini 2.5
model series:
Beyond 2.5 Pro’s incredible performance
on academic benchmarks
, it’s now the world-leading model across the
WebDev Arena
and
LMArena
leaderboards, and for
helping people learn
.
We’re bringing new capabilities to 2.5 Pro and 2.5 Flash: native audio output for a more natural conversational experience, advanced security safeguards, and
Project Mariner
’s computer use capabilities. 2.5 Pro will get even better with
Deep Think
, an experimental, enhanced reasoning mode for highly-complex math and coding.
We continue to invest in the developer experience, introducing thought summaries in the
Gemini API
and in
Vertex AI
for more transparency, extending thinking budgets to 2.5 Pro for more control, and adding support for MCP tools in the Gemini API and
SDK
for access to more open source tools.
2.5 Flash is now available to everyone in the
Gemini app
, and we'll make our updated version generally available in
Google AI Studio
for developers and in
Vertex AI
for enterprises in early June, with 2.5 Pro soon after.
This remarkable progress is the result of the relentless effort of teams across Google to improve our technologies, and develop and release them safely and responsibly. Let’s dive in.
2.5 Pro performs better than ever
We recently
updated 2.5 Pro
to help developers build richer, interactive web apps. It’s great to see the
positive reaction from users and developers
and we’re continuing to make improvements based on user feedback.
In addition to its strong performance on academic benchmarks, the new 2.5 Pro is now leading the popular coding leaderboard,
WebDev Arena
, with an ELO score of 1415. It’s also leading across all leaderboards of the
LMArena
, which evaluates human preference in various dimensions. And, with its 1 million-token context window, 2.5 Pro has state-of-the-art
long context and video understanding performance
.
Since incorporating LearnLM, our family of models built with educational experts, 2.5 Pro is also now the
leading model for learning
. In head-to-head comparisons evaluating its pedagogy and effectiveness, educators and experts preferred Gemini 2.5 Pro over other models across a diverse range of scenarios. And, it
outperformed top models
on every one of the
five principles of learning science
used to build AI systems for learning.
Read more in our updated
Gemini 2.5 Pro model card
and on the
Gemini technology page
.
Deep Think
Through exploring the frontiers of Gemini’s thinking capabilities, we’re starting to test an enhanced reasoning mode called
Deep Think
that uses new research techniques enabling the model to consider multiple hypotheses before responding.
2.5 Pro Deep Think gets an impressive score on
2025 USAMO
, currently one of the hardest math benchmarks. It also leads on
LiveCodeBench
, a difficult benchmark for competition-level coding, and scores 84.0% on
MMMU
, which tests multimodal reasoning.
Because we're defining the frontier with 2.5 Pro DeepThink, we're taking extra time to conduct more frontier safety evaluations and get further input from safety experts. As part of that, we’re going to make it available to trusted testers via the
Gemini API
to get their feedback before making it widely available.
An even better 2.5 Flash
2.5 Flash
is our most efficient workhorse model designed for speed and low-cost — and it’s now better across many dimensions. It’s improved across key benchmarks for reasoning, multimodality, code and long context while getting even more efficient, using 20-30% less tokens in our evaluations.
The new 2.5 Flash is now available for preview in
Google AI Studio
for developers, in
Vertex AI
for enterprise and in the
Gemini app
for everyone. And in early June, it’ll be generally available for production.
Read more in our updated
Gemini 2.5 Flash model card
and on the
Gemini technology page
.
New Gemini 2.5 capabilities
Native audio output and improvements to Live API
Today, the
Live API
is introducing a preview version of audio-visual input and native audio out dialogue, so you can directly build conversational experiences, with a more natural and expressive Gemini.
It also allows the user to steer its tone, accent and style of speaking. For example, you can tell the model to use a

• **russfink** 提出一个技术性建议，询问公司为何不发布AI生成答案的哈希值，以便像教师这样的用户能够验证AI是否生成了特定的结果。

补充讨论：
• **关于模型表现的争议**：cye131和Aeolun都对新模型的实际表现提出了质疑，前者基于技术细节和任务表现，后者基于个人使用体验。

• **关于版本更新的争议**：mchusma对版本频繁更新持批评态度，认为这增加了不必要的复杂性，而Aeolun则赞赏Claude模型在更新上的谨慎态度。

• **关于验证机制的讨论**：russfink提出的哈希值建议引发了对AI生成结果验证机制的讨论，这是一个技术性和实用性兼具的问题。

data.title: The Windows Subsystem for Linux is now open source
data.author: pentagrama
data.article_summary: 2025年5月19日，微软在Microsoft Build大会上宣布Windows Subsystem for Linux（WSL）正式开源。WSL的代码已在GitHub上的Microsoft/WSL仓库中发布，用户可以下载源码、添加新功能和修复问题，参与WSL的开发。WSL由多个组件组成，包括命令行工具（如wsl.exe）、WSL服务（wslservice.exe）、Linux初始化进程等。虽然部分组件（如Lxcore.sys和P9rdr.sys）仍未开源，但其他如WSL2的Linux内核和WSLg已早先开源。WSL最初于2016年发布，历经多次改进，从WSL 1演变到基于真实Linux内核的WSL 2，并逐步添加了对GPU、图形应用和systemd的支持。2021年，WSL从Windows代码库中分离，作为独立包发布，并于2022年发布稳定版WSL 1.0.0。开源WSL旨在加速其发展，回馈社区的长期支持与贡献。当前最新版本为WSL 2.5.7，未来将继续演进。

44031385.article_content:
Microsoft Build
May 19, 2025
The Windows Subsystem for Linux is now open source
By
Pierre Boulay
Today we’re very excited to announce the open-source release of the Windows Subsystem for Linux. This is the result of a multiyear effort to prepare for this, and a great closure to the first ever issue raised on the Microsoft/WSL repo:
Will this be Open Source? · Issue #1 · microsoft/WSL
.
That means that the code that powers WSL is now available on GitHub at
Microsoft/WSL
and open sourced to the community! You can download WSL and build it from source, add new fixes and features and participate in WSL’s active development.
WSL component overview
WSL is made of a set of distribution components. Some run in Windows, and some run inside the WSL 2 virtual machine. Here’s an overview of WSL’s architecture:
WSL’s code can be broken up into these main areas:
Command line executables that are the entry points to interact with WSL
wsl.exe, wslconfig.exe and wslg.exe
The WSL service that starts the WSL VM, starts distros, mounts file access shares and more
wslservice.exe
Linux init and daemon processes, binaries that run in Linux to provide WSL functionality
init for start up, gns for networking, localhost for port forwarding, etc.
File sharing Linux files to Windows with WSL’s plan9 server implementation
plan9
Head over to
https://wsl.dev
to learn more about each component.
This comes as an addition to the already open sourced WSL components:
microsoft/wslg: Enabling the Windows Subsystem for Linux to include support for Wayland and X server related scenarios
microsoft/WSL2-Linux-Kernel: The source for the Linux kernel used in Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2)
The following components are still part of the Windows image and are not open sourced at this time:
Lxcore.sys, the kernel side driver that powers WSL 1
P9rdr.sys and p9np.dll, which runs the “\\wsl.localhost” filesystem redirection (from Windows to Linux)
Why open source now? A bit of history…
WSL was first announced at BUILD back in 2016 and first shipped with the Windows 10 Anniversary update.
At that time WSL was based on a pico process provider, lxcore.sys, which enabled Windows to natively run ELF executables, and implement Linux syscalls inside the Windows kernel. This eventually became what we today know as “WSL 1”, which WSL still supports.
Over time it became clear that the best way to provide optimal compatibility with native Linux was to rely on the Linux kernel itself. WSL 2 was born, and first announced in 2019.
As the community behind WSL grew, WSL gained more features such as GPU support, graphical applications support (via wslg) and support for systemd.
It eventually became clear that to keep up with the growing community and feature requests, WSL had to move faster, and ship separately from Windows. That’s why in 2021 we separated WSL from the Windows codebase, and moved it to its own codebase. This new WSL first shipped as version 0.47.1 to the Microsoft Store, in July 2021. At the time, only Windows 11 was supported, and the package was marked as preview, only recommended to users that wanted to experience the latest and greatest of WSL.
We continued to develop this new “WSL package” until it was ready for general availability. That happened November of 2022, with WSL 1.0.0, which added support for Windows 10 and was the first “stable” release of this new WSL.
From there we kept on improving WSL, with the objective of fully transitioning all users to this new WSL package, and away from the WSL component that shipped with Windows. Windows 11 24H2 was the first Windows build that moved users from the “built-in” WSL to the “new” WSL package. We kept wsl.exe in the Windows image, so it could download the latest package on demand to make the transition easier.
As we kept on improving WSL, we eventually hit another milestone: WSL 2.0.0 (What are the three hardest problems in computer science? Off by one errors and naming things!).
WSL 2.0.0 introduced major improvements such as mirrored networking, DNS tunneling, session 0 support, proxy support, firewall support and more.
And that’s the milestone we’re still building on today! At the time of writing this article, WSL
2.5.7
is the latest available version out of our
nine pages of Github releases
since 0.47.1 4 years ago !
The community behind WSL
Over the years we’ve been incredibly lucky to have a strong community supporting WSL from day 1. We’ve been blessed with people sharing their knowledge, and spending countless hours to help track down bugs, find the best ways to implement new features and improve WSL.
WSL could never have been what it is today without its community. Even without access to WSL’s source code, people have been able to make major contributions that lead to what WSL is now.
This is why we’re incredibly excited to open-source WSL today. We’ve seen how much the community has contributed to WSL without access to the source code, and we can’t wait to see how WSL will evolve now t

data.author: bekacru
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Better Auth 库的优点、功能需求、与其他解决方案的比较以及对未来发展的担忧和建议。

不同观点：
• **对Better Auth的高度评价**：
  - jamesjulich：赞赏Better Auth团队快速修复漏洞，社区领导力强，开发速度快，使用灵活，文档完善。
  - primitivesuave：认为Better Auth是TypeScript开发者的最佳选择，已经在生产应用中使用，文档完善。
  - hyuuu：长期用户，赞赏支持的响应速度，推荐该框架。
  - theogravity：对Better Auth的灵活性和功能性表示期待，尤其是在多账号切换和JWT刷新等问题上。

• **功能需求和改进建议**：
  - nikcub：建议移除主页上的不当语言，以避免被防火墙列入黑名单。
  - macklemoreshair：指出缺乏SCIM支持，这对争取企业客户是一个障碍。
  - twodave：询问是否支持动态登录提供者URL，以满足特定客户的安全需求。
  - sberens：认为虽然"不要自己造轮子"的说法在过去适用，但现在有了丰富的参考资料和核心库，建议提供可修改的认证原语。

• **与其他解决方案的比较**：
  - XavierPladevall：赞赏Better Auth允许将用户数据存储在自己的数据库中，解决了Clerk的数据锁定问题。
  - davedx：比较了Better Auth与Keycloak和Ory Kratos，指出Better Auth在数据集成上的优势，但后者在自托管和独立环境运行上也有其优点。

• **对未来发展的担忧**：
  - akouri：作为Better Auth的长期用户，担心其在获得风投资金后是否会改变，对未来使用持谨慎态度。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现细节**：
  - clgeoio：指出在使用边缘框架（如Cloudflare Workers）时，CLI工具的开发体验较差，环境变量在构建时未知。

争议焦点：
• **功能完善性**：一些用户关注Better Auth在企业级功能（如SCIM支持）和动态URL处理上的不足，而其他用户则对其现有的灵活性和功能表示满意。

• **未来发展方向**：用户akouri对Better Auth获得风投资金后的发展方向表示担忧，而其他用户则对其当前的表现和未来功能扩展持积极态度。

总结：Better Auth在社区中获得了广泛的好评，尤其在灵活性和开发速度上。然而，用户也提出了一些功能需求和改进建议，特别是在企业级支持和动态URL处理方面。此外，部分用户对其未来的发展方向表示关注。

data.title: Show HN: I made an app to create personalized stories for children in 5 minutes
data.author: xcanchal
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个可以快速定制个性化故事的在线服务。用户可以通过四个简单步骤在5分钟内创建并下载一本专属故事书：配置角色、主题和插图风格，生成故事文本，选择和调整插图，最后下载PDF文件。该服务适合各个年龄段的儿童，故事内容会根据角色年龄自动调整。用户可以多次生成新故事，但完成后无法再编辑。该服务还提供多种插图风格选择，并且在旅途中也可轻松使用。目前提供首次故事20%的优惠。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成儿童书籍项目的价值与影响

不同观点：
• **反对AI生成儿童书籍**：
  - [sambeau] 认为儿童书籍是艺术品，能够滋养、娱乐、教育孩子，并培养道德和幽默感。AI生成书籍不仅剽窃了当代和历史上艺术家的创作，还对人类文化和自然环境造成破坏。该评论质疑这种项目的意义，认为它仅仅是为了金钱或网络关注。
  - [gambiting] 强烈反对此类服务，指出像Spotify等平台已经被AI生成的儿童故事淹没，难以找到有灵魂的作品。作为家长，评论者认为AI生成内容像癌症一样扩散，呼吁停止这种项目。

• **对项目持谨慎态度**：
  - [tanvach] 预见到该项目会引发两极分化的意见，但对项目表示一定的理解。虽然AI工具可以吸引非专业人士快速实现目标，但评论者强调书籍创作过程中的亲子活动（如一起画画、去图书馆等）才是创造记忆和意义的核心，AI应该辅助这些活动，而不是取代它们。

• **技术与使用体验问题**：
  - [tropdrop] 对项目中的词汇选择提出疑问，认为应该根据儿童年龄调整词汇难度。
  - [flippinbits] 对网站的购买功能提出批评，指出结账功能无法正常工作（500错误响应）。

• **质疑项目的独特性与价值**：

data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 本文提供了各种加密货币的最新价格及涨跌幅。以比特币（BTC）为例，其价格为106,301美元，涨幅0.93%。以太坊（ETH）价格为2,499.70美元，下跌0.49%。其他主要加密货币如XRP、BNB、SOL等也有不同程度的涨跌。同时，文章列出了多种稳定币如USDC、USDT等的价格及其微小波动。整体来看，市场波动不大，部分币种如AAVE、QNT、PENDLE等有较显著涨幅，而如LDO、DOGE、MATIC等则出现明显下跌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Coinbase数据泄露与传统金融公司在保护客户信息上的比较，以及KYC（了解你的客户）法规的必要性。

不同观点：
• ecshafer认为传统金融公司（如Vanguard）在保护客户信息方面已经非常成熟，限制员工访问敏感信息，并且所有操作都有记录和追踪。相比之下，Coinbase在处理数据泄露事件时表现出不成熟，并将责任归咎于“海外”员工是不负责任的。传统金融公司已经解决了这些问题，而Coinbase等公司尚未达到同样的标准。

• tabbott反驳了一些文章中将数据泄露的部分责任归咎于KYC法规的说法，认为这是“自私的胡说八道”。他认为社会有权要求金融机构既要保护客户的敏感信息，又要遵守KYC规定以打击洗钱活动。特别是在Coinbase这样连接加密货币和传统货币系统的机构中，KYC是必要的。

补充讨论：
• ecshafer通过个人在Vanguard工作的经验，提供了具体例子说明传统金融公司如何严格管理客户信息访问权限，强调了这些公司成熟的安全措施和内部控制。
• tabbott则关注KYC法规的必要性，认为这些规定对于打击金融犯罪是不可或缺的，并暗示不能以保护客户信息不力为借口来削弱KYC的要求。
• 争议的焦点在于Coinbase数据泄露的责任归属和KYC法规的合理性。ecshafer认为Coinbase在管理和安全措施上不成熟，而tabbott则认为将问题归咎于KYC法规是不合理的，强调了法规在防止洗钱中的重要性。

data.title: Microsoft-backed Builder.ai enters insolvency proceedings
data.author: upupupandaway
data.article_summary: AI软件公司Builder.ai正在进入破产程序，该公司发言人向TechCrunch证实。这家获得微软支持的独角兽企业曾融资超过4.5亿美元，以其简化应用程序和网站开发的AI平台而闻名。然而，由于历史挑战和过去决策导致的财务压力，公司无法恢复。Builder.ai近期经历了高层变动和财务问题，包括调低2024年收入预期以及前员工指控销售数据造假。此前，公司曾因声称其平台高度自动化但实际依赖人工工程师而引发争议。公司表示将与管理人合作，支持员工、客户和合作伙伴度过难关，并探索业务重组的可能选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一家公司是否应在快速增长和财务稳健之间保持平衡

不同观点：
• Stephen_hn 对公司烧钱速度表示质疑，认为在两年内花掉2.5亿而没有预留应急资金是不明智的。他质疑公司是否缺乏财务知识，或者仅仅是过于乐观，想通过烧钱来增加成功机会。
  - 论据：公司在两年内烧掉2.5亿，却没有考虑留出5000万至1亿作为应急资金。
  - 例子：具体提到文章中公司筹集了4.5亿，而官网显示2023年筹集了2.5亿。

• 隐含观点一：可能公司缺乏财务管理能力。
  - 论据：Stephen_hn 怀疑公司是否没有财务知识，暗示可能存在财务管理不善的问题。

• 隐含观点二：公司可能故意采取高风险策略，以快速增长为目标。
  - 论据：Stephen_hn 提到公司可能非常乐观，想通过快速烧钱来增加成功机会。
  - 争议点：Stephen_hn 对这种策略是否真的能提供最好的机会表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于公司烧钱策略的合理性。一方认为应该有更谨慎的财务规划，预留应急资金；另一方（假设的公司决策者）可能认为高风险高回报，通过快速烧钱能增加成功几率。

• Stephen_hn 的评论反映了对公司财务管理的关注，质疑这种激进烧钱策略是否真的能带来最好的结果，但同时也保留了对公司决策者可能有其他考虑的理解。

44042963.article_content:
AI software company Builder.ai is entering insolvency proceedings, a company spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch.
The Microsoft-backed unicorn, which has raised more than $450 million in funding, rose to prominence for its AI-based platform that aimed to simplify the process of building apps and websites.
According to the spokesperson, Builder.ai, also known as Engineer.ai Corporation, is appointing an administrator to “manage the company’s affairs.”
“Despite the tireless efforts of our current team and exploring every possible option, the business has been unable to recover from historic challenges and past decisions that placed significant strain on its financial position,” the company said in a statement. “Our immediate priority is to support our employees, customers, and partners through this difficult time. We will work closely with the appointed administrators to ensure an orderly process and to explore all available options for parts of the business, where possible.”
Builder.ai has faced major leadership shakeups and financial issues over the past few months. In March, it was
reported
that the company last summer lowered its estimated revenue by 25% for the second half of 2024. In February, the company appointed a new CEO, Manpreet Ratia.
Builder.ai hired auditors to study its financials, indicating that something may have been off behind the scenes. According to
Bloomberg
, former employees alleged that the company had inflated sales figures by more than 20% on multiple occasions.
Before
Engineer.ai
largely rebranded to
Builder.ai
, it attracted a minor scandal.
Engineer.ai
claimed to have built a largely automated app development platform, but the platform in truth relied heavily on human engineers, according to
The Wall Street Journal
.

data.title: Lyria 2
data.author: georgehill
data.article_summary: Lyria 2是最新推出的高保真音乐生成模型，能够生成专业级音质的音乐，支持多种音乐风格和复杂编曲。该模型由音乐人和制作人共同开发，允许用户通过文本提示控制音乐的风格、调性、BPM等细节，提供精细的创作控制。Lyria 2不仅能帮助音乐人加速创作过程，克服创作障碍，还能探索新的音乐风格和技术。配套工具Music AI Sandbox为音乐创作提供了新的实验平台，并通过与艺术家的合作确保工具的实用性和责任性。Lyria 2还集成了隐私和安全技术，如数字水印工具SynthID，以确保AI生成内容的识别和安全。目前，该模型正处于有限测试阶段，感兴趣的用户可以加入等待名单。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在音乐创作中的应用及其对音乐人就业的影响

不同观点：
• [vunderba的观点] 他认为现有的AI工具更多关注通过文本提示生成新音乐或帮助创作新作品，但他个人需要的是一种可以对已有旋律进行补充和完善的工具，例如自动添加伴奏或生成打击乐层。他强调这种功能对于音乐人来说更有趣且实用，而不是完全依赖AI生成新音乐。

• [rafram的观点] 他批评AI销售人员对AI在音乐创作中的作用存在误解，认为AI不是帮助现有艺术家减少工作量，而是让非专业人士能够生成简单的音乐，从而取代原本可能由专业音乐人承担的工作。他担忧这种趋势会减少音乐人的就业机会，特别是那些依赖于制作简单背景音乐的工作。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点] 核心争议在于AI在音乐创作中的角色及其对音乐人职业的潜在影响。一方面，AI工具可以为艺术家提供创作的起点或突破创作瓶颈；另一方面，这类工具也可能导致音乐人失去一些工作机会，尤其是那些以制作简单音乐为主的职业。

• [具体例子] vunderba提到希望有AI工具能够分析现有旋律并添加伴奏或打击乐，而rafram则担心AI会让非专业人士生成低质量的音乐，从而取代专业音乐人的工作，特别是在背景音乐和简单音乐制作领域。

• [对AI的不同期望] vunderba对AI在音乐创作中的期望更偏向于辅助工具，帮助音乐人丰富已有作品；而rafram则关注AI对音乐行业就业市场的冲击，担心其可能导致音乐人失业。

Powerful composition, endless exploration
Lyria 2 is an advanced AI model, developed with input and insights from musicians and producers. Artists can use text prompts to shape the music, while controlling the key, BPM, and other characteristics.
High-fidelity music
Generates music with remarkable detail and richness, capturing nuance across different instruments and playing styles. Produces professional-grade 48kHz stereo audio, ready for seamless integration into any project.
Granular creative control
Allows musicians to control fine details within their compositions, so they can create pieces that match their intent and vision.
Diverse musical possibilities
Allows composition across a wide range of genres and styles. Classical, jazz, pop, electronic — musicians can steer compositions towards their tastes, and explore diverse musical ideas along the way.
The sound of possibility
Musicians can create pieces in countless styles using Lyria 2. Here are a few examples to showcase its potential range.
Your creative partner
Keep the music flowing
Lyria 2 can create new starting points, suggest harmonies, or draft longer arrangements. It helps musicians focus on their broader visions — or jump past writer’s block.
Accelerate creativity
Composing complex passages and creating variations on themes can take hours, or even days. Lyria 2 accelerates the process, allowing musicians to bring their musical ideas to life in no time.
Uncover new styles
Discover unfamiliar genres, techniques, and possibilities. Experiment with unexpected melodies and harmonies. Lyria 2 can broaden musical understanding and help people explore new creative avenues.

We created Music AI Sandbox in collaboration with artists. Their input has guided our development, resulting in a set of responsibly-created tools that are practically useful for artists of all levels — opening doors to music creation.

Learn about our previous experiments, in collaboration with artists.
Shankar Mahadevan x Music AI
We teamed up with Grammy Award-winning Indian music icon Shankar Mahadevan to explore the exciting fusion of AI and India’s musical traditions. The music of India, a powerhouse of artistic influence widely known for its vibrant Bollywood and booming regional film industries, draws from traditions like Carnatic, Hindustani, folk, dance and devotional genres. This richness provided the perfect canvas for exploration using our Music AI Sandbox.

The Sound of AI
We partnered with award-winning musicians and composers. Leveraging the Music AI Sandbox, we integrated their instrumental creations to craft the sonic foundation for Google Cloud Next '25. This project showcases AI elevating and expanding human creative possibilities.

We believe AI should enhance human creativity, not replace it. We’re working directly with artists to gather feedback and to develop guardrails that address their concerns. By doing this, we ensure this tool empowers creators and helps them realize the possibilities of AI in their work.

While Lyria 2 demonstrates the incredible potential of AI for music generation, we are still working to develop and refine its performance — and to expand its coverage of languages and genres.

data.article_summary: Gemini Diffusion是实验性文本生成模型，采用扩散技术，提升文本生成的控制力、创造力和速度。与传统自回归模型逐词生成不同，扩散模型通过逐步去除噪声生成文本，具有更快的响应速度和更高的连贯性，还能在生成过程中修正错误。其性能媲美更大规模的模型，在多个基准测试中表现优异，如代码生成和数学推理。目前，该模型作为实验演示开放，用户可申请加入等待名单以获取试用机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：扩散模型在文本生成中的应用及其技术难点

不同观点：
• Diffusion models的工作原理：[minimaxir]指出，扩散模型通过逐步优化噪声来生成输出，而不是直接预测文本。这种方法允许模型快速迭代和纠错，使其在编辑任务中表现出色，尤其是在数学和代码领域。

• 扩散模型在图像和文本生成中的差异：[minimaxir]提到，图像的潜在扩散可以模糊和不精确，而文本输出由于其离散性，必须更加精确。这可能是为什么在技术可用多年后，仍然没有其他人成功开发出优秀的文本扩散模型的原因。

• Google的独特优势：[minimaxir]认为，Google在解决文本扩散模型精确性问题时，使用了一些未公开的技术（"secret sauce"），并且对这些技术严格保密，这使得其他开发者难以复制其成功。

补充讨论：
• 技术保密与竞争优势：[minimaxir]的评论暗示了Google在文本扩散模型领域的领先地位可能部分归因于其对关键技术的保密，从而在竞争中保持优势。

• 扩散模型在不同领域应用的挑战：评论指出了扩散模型在处理图像和文本不同需求时的技术难点，强调了文本生成需要更高精度的事实。

争议焦点：
• 扩散模型技术公开与商业机密之间的平衡：一方面，技术进步依赖于知识的共享和开放；另一方面，企业需要保护其竞争优势，这可能导致关键技术的保密，从而影响整个领域的进展。

Gemini Diffusion
Our state-of-the-art, experimental text diffusion model
Join the waitlist
Large-language models are the foundation of generative AI today. We’re using a technique called diffusion to explore a new kind of language model that gives users greater control, creativity, and speed in text generation.
What is a diffusion model?
Capabilities
Benchmarks
Hands-on
What is a diffusion model?
Traditional autoregressive language models generate text one word – or token – at a time. This sequential process can be slow, and limit the quality and coherence of the output.
Diffusion models work differently. Instead of predicting text directly, they learn to generate outputs by refining noise, step-by-step. This means they can iterate on a solution very quickly and error correct during the generation process. This helps them excel at tasks like editing, including in the context of math and code.

Rapid response
Generates content significantly faster than even our fastest model so far.
More coherent text
Generates entire blocks of tokens at once, meaning it responds more coherently to a user’s prompt than autoregressive models.
Iterative refinement
Corrects errors during generation for more consistent outputs.

Gemini Diffusion’s external benchmark performance is comparable to much larger models, whilst also being faster.

data.title: Zod 4
data.author: bpierre
data.article_summary:
Zod 4 是一个经过一年开发后发布的稳定版本，具有更快的速度、更精简的代码库以及更高的 TypeScript 效率。它解决了许多 Zod 3 的设计限制，并实现了多个备受期待的功能，包括显著的性能提升和减少类型实例化。Zod 4 最初与 Zod 3 一同发布为 `zod@3.25`，用户可以通过升级到 `zod@^3.25.0` 并从 `"/v4"` 子路径导入来使用 Zod 4。未来将发布 `zod@4.0.0`，并从包根目录导出。

新版本在字符串解析上快 14 倍，数组解析快 7 倍，对象解析快 6.5 倍，并大幅减少了 TypeScript 类型实例化次数。通过重新设计泛型，Zod 4 还避免了某些复杂的类型实例化问题。详细的迁移指南和功能介绍可参阅官方文档和迁移指南。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zod库的版本管理、生态系统兼容性、与其他工具的比较以及在实际开发中的应用和挑战。

不同观点：
• [colinmcd] 认为Zod面临独特的约束，因为许多其他库直接引用了Zod的接口和类，导致Zod发布重大版本更新时会引发“版本雪崩”。为了解决这个问题，采用了类似Golang的版本管理方法，通过子路径来管理不同版本的兼容性，从而减轻对生态系统的破坏。
• [rafram] 对npm的依赖管理系统持批评态度，认为peer dependencies存在问题，并指出Zod 4通过伪装成v3来简化迁移过程。
• [myflash13] 表示自己不使用SPA或JS前端框架，因此没有使用Zod/ArkType的需求，并认为这样可以避免很多复杂性问题，暗示这种复杂性可能是不必要的。
• [causal] 认为Zod这样的显式验证工具反映了现代Web开发中的重复工作问题，需要在多个地方描述相同的结构，感到繁琐。
• [satvikpendem] 认为ArkType在速度和TypeScript的 ergonomics 上优于Zod，并基于这些因素选择了ArkType。
• [8s2ngy] 对Zod新版本的重大变化感到担忧，认为对老项目来说迁移任务艰巨，尤其是需要保持多个库的同步和功能正常。
• [punkpeye] 对Zod 4的发布持积极态度，赞赏作者的解决方案，认为这样可以让开发者立即开始使用新版本而不必等待所有依赖更新。
• [neilpa] 正在评估Zod和ArkType，但对Zod的语法与TypeScript类型的定义差异感到困惑，询问选择Zod的理由。
• [sroussey] 希望有人能比较Zod4和TypeBox，指出TypeBox的JSON Schema互操作性是一个优点。
• [CGamesPlay] 对Zod 4引入的zod/v4-mini import表示担忧，认为可能会增加bundle大小，建议如果zod/v4能作为zod/v4-mini的包装会更好。

补充讨论：
• [johnfn] 提出如何处理服务器返回的复杂类型的问题，特别是使用 discriminated union 来解决不同API端点返回不同类型数据的问题，并提到过去通过normalize函数解决，但这种方式很快变得混乱。
• [varbhat] 建议使用JSON-Schema和AJV库，认为这样可以在非TypeScript语言中实现验证器，询问Zod与JSON-Schema的比较。
• [labadal] 表示刚在项目中使用Zod，认为Zod 4的发布时机很好，避免了大量迁移工作。
• [90s_dev] 询问是否有关于TypeScript-first schema validation和静态类型推断的比较指南，之前使用过io-ts和ajv。

争议焦点：
• Zod 4的版本管理和兼容性策略是否有效解决了“版本雪崩”问题，还是引入了新的复杂性（如zod/v4-mini的引入可能增加bundle大小）。
• 对于开发者而言，Zod与ArkType、TypeBox等类似工具的选择依据和优劣比较。

Introducing Zod 4
After a year of active development: Zod 4 is now stable! It's faster, slimmer, more
tsc
-efficient, and implements some long-requested features.
❤️
Huge thanks to
Clerk
, who supported my work on Zod 4 through their extremely generous
OSS Fellowship
. They were an amazing partner throughout the (much longer than anticipated!) development process.
Versioning
To simplify the migration process both for users and Zod's ecosystem of associated libraries, Zod 4 will initially published alongside Zod 3 as part of the
zod@3.25
release. Despite the version number, it it considered stable and ready for production use.
To upgrade:
npm upgrade zod@^3.25.0
Then import Zod 4 from the
"/v4"
subpath:
import
{ z }
from
"zod/v4"
;
Down the road, when there's broad support for Zod 4, we'll publish
zod@4.0.0
on npm. At this point, Zod 4 will be exported from the package root (
"zod"
). The
"zod/v4"
subpath will remain available. For a detailed writeup on the reasons for this versioning scheme, refer to
this issue
.
For a complete list of breaking changes, refer to the
Migration guide
. This post focuses on new features & enhancements.
Why a new major version?
Zod v3.0 was released in May 2021 (!). Back then Zod had 2700 stars on GitHub and 600k weekly downloads. Today it has 37.8k stars and 31M weekly downloads (up from 23M when the beta came out 6 weeks ago!). After 24 minor versions, the Zod 3 codebase had hit a ceiling; the most commonly requested features and improvements require breaking changes.
Zod 4 fixes a number of long-standing design limitations of Zod 3 in one fell swoop, paving the way for several long-requested features and a huge leap in performance. It closes 9 of Zod's
10 most upvoted open issues
. With luck, it will serve as the new foundation for many more years to come.
For a scannable breakdown of what's new, see the table of contents. Click on any item to jump to that section.
